# Authentication

* API Key (apiToken)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. Like many other API providers, it’s also possible to generate API Tokens to be used (in HTTP Header) for authentication. An API token ties to a Admin with equal or less privileges.

**Notes**:
* an API token generated for a specific admin has the same privilege as the user
* an API token will be automatically removed if not used for > 90 days

SSO admins cannot generate these API tokens. Refer Org level API tokens which can have privileges of a specific Org/Site for more information.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic While our current UI uses Session / Cookie-based authentication, it’s also possible to do Basic Auth.

<h1 id="mist-api-login">Login</h1>

## login

<a id="opIdlogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "string",
    "password": "string",
    "two_factor": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/login`

Log in with email/password

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "string",
  "password": "string",
  "two_factor": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="login-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string|true|none|
|» password|body|string|true|none|
|» two_factor|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "email": "test@mistsys.com",
  "two_factor_passed": false,
  "two_factor_required": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "sso admin login needs to be initiated by IdP",
  "forward_url": "https://my.sso/idp_sso_url"
}
```

<h3 id="login-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Login Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Login Failed|Inline|

<h3 id="login-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|string|false|none|none|
|two_factor_passed|boolean|false|none|none|
|two_factor_required|boolean|false|none|none|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|detail|string|true|none|none|
|forward_url|string|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Set-Cookie|string||Session Cookie if login/password authentication is successful|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="mist-api-login-with-oauth2">Login With OAuth2</h1>

A Mist account can be linked to OAuth2 providers:
1. First, login with your Mist account
2. Obtain the Authorization URL for Linking
  1. in JSON response, more usable for developers. Simply don’t specify the forward parameter when obtaining the authorization URL 
  2. or as GET parameter, for UI where the user flow can be continued. Specify the landing page/url of your choice
3. Obtain the authorizaiton code by clicking / going through Authorization URL
Link Mist Account against OAuth2 Provider by using the authorization code

## provisionInstallerDevices

<a id="opIdprovisionInstallerDevices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/installer/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/0000000000ab \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "deviceprofile_name": "string",
    "for_site": true,
    "height": 0,
    "map_id": "09d2b626-2e4e-45ef-a3c4-e6aeb6c83db1",
    "name": "string",
    "orientation": 0,
    "site_id": "72771e6a-6f5e-4de4-a5b9-1266c4197811",
    "site_name": "string",
    "x": 0,
    "y": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v1/installer/orgs/{org_id}/devices/{device_mac}`

Provision or Replace a device 

If replacing_mac is in the request payload, other attributes are ignored, we attempt to replace existing device (with mac replacing_mac) with the inventory device being configured. The replacement device must be in the inventory but not assigned, and the replacing_mac device must be assigned to a site, and satisfy grace period requirements. The Device replaced will become unassigned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "deviceprofile_name": "string",
  "for_site": true,
  "height": 0,
  "map_id": "09d2b626-2e4e-45ef-a3c4-e6aeb6c83db1",
  "name": "string",
  "orientation": 0,
  "site_id": "72771e6a-6f5e-4de4-a5b9-1266c4197811",
  "site_name": "string",
  "x": 0,
  "y": 0
}
```

<h3 id="provisioninstallerdevices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_mac|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[Installer_devices](#schemainstaller_devices)|false|Request Body|
|» deviceprofile_name|body|string|false|none|
|» height|body|number|false|none|
|» map_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» orientation|body|number|false|none|
|» replacing_mac|body|string|false|Onlif this is to replace an existing device|
|» role|body|string|false|optional role for switch / gateway|
|» site_name|body|string|false|none|
|» x|body|number|false|none|
|» y|body|number|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "invalid replacing_mac"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "replacing_mac inventory not found"
}
```

<h3 id="provisioninstallerdevices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|Inline|

<h3 id="provisioninstallerdevices-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|detail|string|true|none|none|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|detail|string|false|none|none|

</aside>

## createOrUpdateInstallerSites

<a id="opIdcreateOrUpdateInstallerSites"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/installer/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/sites/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "1601 S. Deanza Blvd., Cupertino, CA, 95014",
    "country_code": "US",
    "latlng": {
      "lat": 37.295833,
      "lng": -122.032946
    },
    "name": "string",
    "rftemplate_name": "rftemplate1",
    "sitegroup_names": [
      "sg1",
      "sg2"
    ],
    "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v1/installer/orgs/{org_id}/sites/{site_name}`

Often the Installers are asked to assign Devices to Sites. The Sites can either be pre-created or created/modified by the Installer. If this is an update, the same grace period also applies.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "1601 S. Deanza Blvd., Cupertino, CA, 95014",
  "country_code": "US",
  "latlng": {
    "lat": 37.295833,
    "lng": -122.032946
  },
  "name": "string",
  "rftemplate_name": "rftemplate1",
  "sitegroup_names": [
    "sg1",
    "sg2"
  ],
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles"
}
```

<h3 id="createorupdateinstallersites-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|site_name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[site](#schemasite)|false|Request Body|
|» |body|string(uuid)|false|Site Template ID|
|» address|body|string|false|full address of the site|
|» alarmtemplate_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Alarm Template ID, this takes precedence over the Org-level alarmtemplate_id|
|» aptemplate_id|body|string|false|AP Template ID, used by APs|
|» country_code|body|string|false|country code for the site (for AP config generation), in two-character|
|» gatewaytemplate_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Gateway Template ID, used by gateways|
|» latlng|body|object|false|site location|
|» » lat|body|number|false|latitude|
|» » lng|body|number|false|longitude|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» networktemplate_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Network Template ID, this takes precedence over Site Settings|
|» notes|body|string|false|optional, any notes about the site|
|» rftemplate_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|RF Template ID, this takes precedence over Site Settings|
|» secpolicy_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|SecPolicy ID|
|» sitegroup_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|sitegroups this site belongs to|
|» timezone|body|string|false|Timezone the site is at|

> Example responses

```json
{}
```

## importInstallerMap

<a id="opIdimportInstallerMap"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/installer/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/sites/string/maps/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'csv=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'json={"import_all_floorplans":false,"import_height":false,"import_orientation":false,"vendor_name":"ekahau"}'
```

`POST /api/v1/installer/orgs/{org_id}/sites/{site_name}/maps/import`

Import data from files is a multipart POST which has an file, an optional json, and an optional csv, to create floorplan, assign & place ap if name or mac matches

> Body parameter

```yaml
csv: string
file: string
json:
  import_all_floorplans: false
  import_height: false
  import_orientation: false
  vendor_name: ekahau
```

|» file|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» json|body|object|false|none|

|» » import_height|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » import_orientation|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » vendor_name|body|string|true|none|

|» default_role|body|string|false|default role to assign if there’s no match. By default, an assertion is treated as invalid when there’s no role matched|

|» idp_sso_url|body|string|false|IDP Single-Sign-On URL|
|» idp_type|body|string|false|none|
|» ignore_unmatched_roles|body|boolean|false|ignore any unmatched roles provided in assertion. By default, an assertion is treated as invalid for any unmatched role|

|» ldap_group_attr|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|

|» ldap_group_filter|body|string|false|if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|» ldap_server_hosts|body|[string]|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_type|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_user_filter|body|string|false|* if `ldap_type`==`ad`: "(CN=%s)"<br>* if `ldap_type`==`okta`: "(uid=%s)"<br>* if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|» name|body|string|true|name|
|» nameid_format|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`saml`|
|» oauth_cc_client_id|body|string|false|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, Client Credentials|
|» oauth_cc_client_secret|body|string|false|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, oauth_cc_client_secret is RSA private key, of the form "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY--...."|
|» oauth_discovery_url|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`oauth`|

|» oauth_tenant_id|body|string|false|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, oauth_tenant_id|
|» oauth_type|body|string|false|none|
|» role_attr_extraction|body|string|false|optional, custom role attribute parsing scheme<br><br>Supported Role Parsing Schemes<br><table><tr><th>Name</th><th>Scheme</th></tr><tr><td>cn</td><td><ul><li>The expected role attribute format in SAML Assertion is “CN=cn,OU=ou1,OU=ou2,…”</li><li>CN (the key) is case insensitive and exactly 1 CN is expected (or the entire entry will be ignored)</li><li>E.g. if role attribute is “CN=cn,OU=ou1,OU=ou2” then parsed role value is “cn”</li></ul></td></tr></table>|
|» role_attr_from|body|string|false| name of the attribute in SAML Assertion to extract role from|
|» type|body|string|false|none|

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs">Orgs</h1>

## createOrg

<a id="opIdcreateOrg"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "alarmtemplate_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
    "allow_mist": true,
    "msp_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
    "name": "string",
    "orggroup_ids": [
      "6f4bf402-45f9-2a56-6c8b-7f83d3bc98e9"
    ],
    "session_expiry": 0
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs`

Org admin can invite people to manage the org. Furthermore, he can dictate the level of security those accounts are. The check is enforced when the invited admin tries to “accept” the invitation and every time the admin tries to login

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alarmtemplate_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "allow_mist": true,
  "msp_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "name": "string",
  "orggroup_ids": [
    "6f4bf402-45f9-2a56-6c8b-7f83d3bc98e9"
  ],
  "session_expiry": 0
}
```

<h3 id="createorg-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[org](#schemaorg)|false|none|
|» alarmtemplate_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|
|» allow_mist|body|boolean|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» orggroup_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|none|
|» session_expiry|body|number|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "alarmtemplate_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "allow_mist": true,
  "created_time": 0,
  "id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "modified_time": 0,
  "msp_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",

  "orggroup_ids": [
    "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1"
  ],
  "session_expiry": 0
}
```

## cloneOrg

<a id="opIdcloneOrg"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/clone \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "New Org"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/clone`

Create an Org by cloning from another one. Org Settings, Templates, Wxlan Tags, Wxlan Tunnels, Wxlan Rules, Org Wlans will be copied. Sites and Site Groups will not be copied, and therefore, the copied template will not be applied to any site/sitegroups.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "New Org"
}
```

<h3 id="cloneorg-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|Request Body|
|» name|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "alarmtemplate_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "allow_mist": true,
  "created_time": 0,
  "id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "modified_time": 0,
  "msp_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "name": "string",
  "orggroup_ids": [
    "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1"
  ],
  "session_expiry": 0
}
```

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs-alarm-templates">Orgs Alarm Templates</h1>

An Alarm Template is a set of Alarm Rules that could be applied to one or more sites (while each site can only pick one Alarm Template), or to the whole org.

## suppressOrgAlarm

<a id="opIdsuppressOrgAlarm"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/alarmtemplates/suppress \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "applies": {
      "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "site_ids": [
        "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
      ],
      "sitegroup_ids": [
        "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
      ]
    },
    "duration": 60
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/alarmtemplates/suppress`

In certain situations, for example, scheduled maintanance, you may want to suspend alarms to be triggered for a period of time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "applies": {
    "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "site_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "sitegroup_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ]
  },
  "duration": 60
}
```

<h3 id="suppressorgalarm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» applies|body|object|true|Object defines the scope (within the org e.g. whole org, and/or some site-groups, and/or some sites) for which the alarm service has to be suppressed for some `duration`|
|» » org_id|body|string(uuid)|true|UUID of the current org (if provided, the alarms will be suppressed at org level)|
|» » site_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|true|List of UUID of the sites within the org (if provided, the alarms will be suppressed for all the mentioned sites under the org)|
|» » sitegroup_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|true|List of UUID of the site groups within the org (if provided, the alarms will be suppressed for all the sites under those site groups)|
|» duration|body|number|false|duration, in seconds|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="suppressorgalarm-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

## updateOrgAlarmTemplate

<a id="opIdupdateOrgAlarmTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/alarmtemplates/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "delivery": {
      "additional_emails": [
        "string"
      ],
      "enabled": true,
      "to_org_admins": true,
      "to_site_admins": true
    },
    "name": "string",
    "rules": {
      "adhoc_network": {
        "delivery": {
          "additional_emails": [
            "string"
          ],
          "enabled": true,
          "to_org_admins": true,
```

<h3 id="updateorgalarmtemplate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|alarmtemplate_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[alarmtemplate](#schemaalarmtemplate)|false|Request Body|
|» delivery|body|[delivery](#schemadelivery)|true|Delivery object to configure the alarm delivery|
|» name|body|string|false|Some string to name the alarm template|
|» rules|body|object|true|Alarm Rules object to configure the individual alarm keys/types. Property key is the alarm name.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » delivery|body|[delivery](#schemadelivery)|false|Delivery object to configure the alarm delivery|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/apitokens`

Create Org API Token
Note that the token key is only available during creation time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "privileges": [
    {
      "role": "admin",
      "scope": "site",
      "site_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "sitegroup_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» privileges|body|[object]|true|list of privileges the token has on the orgs/sites|
|» » role|body|string|true|none|
|» » scope|body|string|true|none|
|» » site_id|body|string(uuid)|true|if `scope`==`site`|
|» » sitegroup_id|body|string(uuid)|false|if `scope`==`sitegroup`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » role|admin|
|» » role|write|
|» » role|read|
|» » scope|site|
|» » scope|org|
|» » scope|sitegroup|

## getOrgAssetFilters

<a id="opIdgetOrgAssetFilters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/assetfilters \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/assetfilters`

Get the list of all BLE asset filters for the given site. Each asset filter in the list operates independently. For a filter object to match an asset, all of the filter properties must match (logical ‘AND’ of each filter property). For example, the “Visitor Tags” filter below will match an asset when both the “ibeacon\_uuid” and “ibeacon_major” properties match the asset. All non-matching assets are ignored.

<h3 id="getorgassetfilters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "ap_mac": "string",
    "beam": 0,
    "created_time": 0,
    "disasbled": true,
    "eddystone_uid_namespace": "2818e3868dec25629ede",
    "eddystone_url": "https://www.abc.com",
    "for_site": true,
    "ibeacon_major": 13,
    "ibeacon_uuid": "f3f17139-704a-f03a-2786-0400279e37c3",
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "mfg_company_id": 935,
    "modified_time": 0,
    "name": "Visitor Tags",
    "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "rssi": 0,
    "service_uuid": "0000fe6a-0000-1000-8000-0030459b3cfb",
    "site_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }
]
```

|200|OK|OK|Inline|

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/assetfilters`

Create Asset Filter

Creates a single BLE asset filter for the given site. Any subset of filter properties can be included in the filter. A matching asset must meet the conditions of all given filter properties (logical ‘AND’).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "created_time": 0,
  "disasbled": true,
  "eddystone_uid_namespace": "string",
  "eddystone_url": "string",
  "for_site": true,
  "ibeacon_major": 0,
  "ibeacon_uuid": "1f89bc00-d0af-481b-82fe-a6629259a39f",
  "id": "430f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cb5bba6f08",
  "mfg_company_id": 0,
  "modified_time": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "org_id": "a40f5d1f-d889-42e9-94ea-b9b33585fc6b",
  "site_id": "72771e6a-6f5e-4de4-a5b9-1266c4197811"
}
```

<h3 id="createorgassetfilters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[asset_filter](#schemaasset_filter)|false|none|
|» ap_mac|body|string|false|none|
|» beam|body|integer|false|none|
|» disasbled|body|boolean|false|whether the asset filter is disabled|
|» eddystone_uid_namespace|body|string|false|eddystone uid namespace used to filter assets|
|» eddystone_url|body|string|false|eddystone url used to filter assets|
|» ibeacon_major|body|integer|false|ibeacon major value used to filter assets|
|» ibeacon_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|ibeacon uuid used to filter assets|
|» mfg_company_id|body|integer|false|ble manufacturing-specific company-id used to filter assets|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» rssi|body|integer|false|none|
|» service_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|ble service data uuid used to filter assets|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "created_time": 0,

  "eddystone_uid_namespace": "string",
  "eddystone_url": "string",
  "for_site": true,
  "ibeacon_major": 0,
  "ibeacon_uuid": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
```

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs-device-profiles">Orgs Device Profiles</h1>

While Templates / RF Templates / Network Templates / Gateway Templates provides powerful ways to control how a Device’s configuration is derived for a Site. There are cases where you’d like another level of control at the Org Level.
A Device Profile contains a subset of Device’s configurations you’d like a device to have. It will be merged at runtime when we’re provisioning an AP.

<h3 id="createorgdeviceprofiles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[deviceprofile](#schemadeviceprofile)|false|Request Body|
|» aeroscout|body|[ap_aeroscout](#schemaap_aeroscout)|false|Aeroscout AP settings|
|» ble_config|body|[ap_ble](#schemaap_ble)|false|BLE AP settings|
|» disable_eth1|body|boolean|false|whether to disable eth1 port|
|» disable_eth2|body|boolean|false|whether to disable eth2 port|
|» disable_eth3|body|boolean|false|whether to disable eth3 port|
|» disable_module|body|boolean|false|whether to disable module port|
|» height|body|number \| null|false|Device Only. Height, in meters, optional|
|» iot_config|body|[ap_iot](#schemaap_iot)|false|IoT AP settings|
|» ip_config|body|[ap_ip](#schemaap_ip)|false|IP AP settings|
|» led|body|[ap_led](#schemaap_led)|false|LED AP settings|
|» map_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Device Only.. Map where the device belongs to|
|» mesh|body|[ap_mesh](#schemaap_mesh)|false|Mesh AP settings|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» notes|body|string \| null|false|Device Only. Any notes about this AP|
|» ntp_servers|body|[string]|false|none|
|» orientation|body|number|false|Device Only. Orientation, 0-359, in degrees, up is 0, right is 90.|
|» orientation_overwrite|body|boolean|false|whether the user overwrite the orientation|
|» poe_passthrough|body|boolean|false|whether to enable power out through module port (for APH) or eth1 (for APL/BT11)|
|» port_config|body|object|false|The property key is the interface(s) name (e.g. "eth1,eth2")|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[ap_port_config](#schemaap_port_config)|false|none|
|» pwr_config|body|object|false|power related configs|
|» » base|body|number|false|additional power to request during negotiating with PSE over PoE, in mW|
|» radio_config|body|[ap_radio](#schemaap_radio)|false|Radio AP settings|
|» switch_config|body|[ap_switch](#schemaap_switch)|false|**Deprecated.** for people who want to fully control the vlans (advanced)|
|» type|body|string|false|none|
|» usb_config|body|[ap_usb](#schemaap_usb)|false|USB AP settings|
|» vars|body|object|false|a dictionary of name->value, the vars can then be used in Wlans. This can overwrite those from Site Vars|
|» x|body|number \| null|false|Device Only. x in pixel|
|» y|body|number \| null|false|Device Only. y in pixel|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|ap|
|» type|switch|
|» type|gateway|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|deviceprofile_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[deviceprofile](#schemadeviceprofile)|false|Request Body|
|» aeroscout|body|[ap_aeroscout](#schemaap_aeroscout)|false|Aeroscout AP settings|
|» ble_config|body|[ap_ble](#schemaap_ble)|false|BLE AP settings|
|» disable_eth1|body|boolean|false|whether to disable eth1 port|
|» disable_eth2|body|boolean|false|whether to disable eth2 port|
|» disable_eth3|body|boolean|false|whether to disable eth3 port|
|» disable_module|body|boolean|false|whether to disable module port|
|» height|body|number \| null|false|Device Only. Height, in meters, optional|
|» iot_config|body|[ap_iot](#schemaap_iot)|false|IoT AP settings|
|» ip_config|body|[ap_ip](#schemaap_ip)|false|IP AP settings|
|» led|body|[ap_led](#schemaap_led)|false|LED AP settings|
|» map_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Device Only.. Map where the device belongs to|
|» mesh|body|[ap_mesh](#schemaap_mesh)|false|Mesh AP settings|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» notes|body|string \| null|false|Device Only. Any notes about this AP|
|» ntp_servers|body|[string]|false|none|
|» orientation|body|number|false|Device Only. Orientation, 0-359, in degrees, up is 0, right is 90.|
|» orientation_overwrite|body|boolean|false|whether the user overwrite the orientation|
|» poe_passthrough|body|boolean|false|whether to enable power out through module port (for APH) or eth1 (for APL/BT11)|
|» port_config|body|object|false|The property key is the interface(s) name (e.g. "eth1,eth2")|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[ap_port_config](#schemaap_port_config)|false|none|
|» pwr_config|body|object|false|power related configs|
|» » base|body|number|false|additional power to request during negotiating with PSE over PoE, in mW|
|» radio_config|body|[ap_radio](#schemaap_radio)|false|Radio AP settings|
|» switch_config|body|[ap_switch](#schemaap_switch)|false|**Deprecated.** for people who want to fully control the vlans (advanced)|
|» type|body|string|false|none|
|» usb_config|body|[ap_usb](#schemaap_usb)|false|USB AP settings|
|» vars|body|object|false|a dictionary of name->value, the vars can then be used in Wlans. This can overwrite those from Site Vars|
|» x|body|number \| null|false|Device Only. x in pixel|
|» y|body|number \| null|false|Device Only. y in pixel|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|ap|
|» type|switch|
|» type|gateway|

```json
      "string"
```

```bash
    "rrm_first_batch_percentage": 2,
    "rrm_max_batch_percentage": 10,

    "rrm_slow_ramp": true,
    "snapshot": false,
    "start_time": 1624399840,

    "version": "3.1.5"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/devices/upgrade`

Upgrade Multiple Sites

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "canary_phases": [
    1,
    10,
    50,
    100
  ],
  "device_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "enable_p2p": true,
  "force": false,
  "max_failure_percentage": 5,
  "max_failures": [
    0
  ],
  "models": [
    "string"
  ],
  "p2p_cluster_size": 0,
  "p2p_parallelism": 0,
  "reboot": false,
  "reboot_at": 1624399840,
  "rrm_first_batch_percentage": 2,
  "rrm_max_batch_percentage": 10,
  "rrm_mesh_upgrade": "string",
  "rrm_node_order": "fringe_to_center",
  "rrm_slow_ramp": true,
  "snapshot": false,
  "start_time": 1624399840,
  "strategy": "big_bang",
  "version": "3.1.5"
}
```

<h3 id="upgradeorgmultisitesdevices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[device_upgrade](#schemadevice_upgrade)|false|none|
|» canary_phases|body|[integer]|false|phases for canary deployment. Each phase represents percentage of AP’s that need to be upgraded. default is [1, 10, 50, 100]|
|» device_ids|body|[string]|false|none|
|» enable_p2p|body|boolean|false|whether to allow local AP-to-AP FW upgrade|
|» force|body|boolean|false|true will force upgrade when requested version is same as running version|
|» max_failure_percentage|body|number|false|percentage of failures allowed across the entire upgrade(not applicable for `big_bang`)|
|» max_failures|body|[integer]|false|number of failures allowed within each phase(applicable for `canary` or `rrm`). Will be used if provided, else max_failure_percentage will be used|
|» models|body|[string]|false|none|
|» p2p_cluster_size|body|integer|false|none|
|» p2p_parallelism|body|integer|false|number of parallel p2p download batches to creat|
|» reboot|body|boolean|false|Reboot device immediately after upgrade is completed (Available on Junos OS devices)|
|» reboot_at|body|number|false|reboot start time in epoch seconds, default is `start_time`|
|» rrm_first_batch_percentage|body|integer|false|percentage of AP’s that need to be present in the first rrm batch|
|» rrm_max_batch_percentage|body|integer|false|max percentage of AP’s that need to be present in each rrm batch|
|» rrm_mesh_upgrade|body|string|false|sequential or parallel (default parallel). Whether to upgrade mesh AP’s parallelly or sequentially at the end of the upgrade|
|» rrm_node_order|body|string|false|Used in rrm to determine whether to start upgrade from fringe or center AP’s|
|» rrm_slow_ramp|body|boolean|false|true will make rrm batch sizes slowly ramp up|
|» snapshot|body|boolean|false|Perform recovery snapshot after device is rebooted (Available on Junos OS devices)|
|» start_time|body|number|false|upgrade start time in epoch seconds, default is now|
|» strategy|body|string|false|`big_bang` (upgrade all at once), `serial` (one at a time), `canary` or `rrm`|
|» version|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» rrm_node_order|fringe_to_center|
|» rrm_node_order|center_to_fringe|
|» strategy|big_bang|
|» strategy|canary|
|» strategy|serial|
|» strategy|rrm|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "470f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f48"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<h3 id="upgradeorgmultisitesdevices-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs-devices-evpn">Orgs Devices EVPN</h1>

EVPN allows an alternative but more efficient LAN architecture utilizing VxLAN / MP-BGP - separating control plane (MAC / IP Learning) from forwarding plane.
In our implementation, following the steps to deploy EVPN topologies in a Site

## createOrgEvpnTopology

<a id="opIdcreateOrgEvpnTopology"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/evpn_topologies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "CC",
    "overwrite": true,
    "pod_names": {
      "1": "default",
      "2": "default"
    },
    "switches": [
      {
        "mac": "5c5b35000003",
        "role": "collapsed-core"
      },
      {
        "mac": "5c5b35000004",
        "role": "collapsed-core"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/evpn_topologies`

While all the `evpn_id` / `downlink_ips` can be specifidd by hand, the easiest way is to call the `build_vpn_topology` API, allowing you to examine the diff, and update it yourself. You can also simply call it with `overwrite=true` which will apply the updates for you.

**Notes:**
1. You can use `core` / `distribution` / `access` to create a CLOS topology
2. You can also use `core` / `distribution` to form a 2-tier EVPN topology where ESI-Lag is configured distribution to connect to access switches
3. In a small/medium campus, `collapsed-core` can be used where core switches are the inter-connected to do EVPN
4. The API uses a few pre-defined parameters and best-practices to generate the configs. It can be customized by using `evpn_options` in Site Setting / Network Template. (e.g. a different subnet for the underlay)

#### Collapsed Core
In a small-medium campus, EVPN can also be enabled only at the core switches (up to 4) by assigning all participating switches with `collapsed-core role`. When there are more than 2 switches, a ring-like topology will be formed.

#### ESI-Lag
If the access switchess does not have EVPN support, you can take advantage of EVPN by setting up ESI-Lag on distribution switches

#### Leaf / Access / Collapsed-Core
For leaf nodes in a EVPN topology, you’d have to configure the IPs for networks that would participate in EVPN. Optionally, VRFs to isolate traffic from one tenant verus another

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "CC",
  "overwrite": true,
  "pod_names": {
    "1": "default",
    "2": "default"
  },
  "switches": [
    {
      "mac": "5c5b35000003",
      "role": "collapsed-core"
    },
    {
      "mac": "5c5b35000004",
      "role": "collapsed-core"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="createorgevpntopology-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[junos_evpn_topology](#schemajunos_evpn_topology)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» pod_names|body|object|false|Property key is the pod number|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» switches|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » deviceprofile_id|body|string|false|none|
|» » esilaglinks|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » evpn_id|body|integer|false|none|
|» » mac|body|string|false|none|
|» » pod|body|integer|false|optionally, for distribution / access / esilag-access, they can be placed into different pods.<br>e.g. <br>* for CLOS, to group dist / access switches into pods<br>* for ERB/CRB, to group dist / esilag-access into pods|
|» » role|body|string|false|use `role`==`none` to remove a switch from the topology|
|» » site_id|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » role|core|
|» » role|distribution|
|» » role|access|
|» » role|collapsed-core|
|» » role|none|
|» » role|esilag-access|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "9197ec96-4c8d-529f-c595-035895e688b2",
  "name": "CC",
  "pod_names": {
    "1": "default",
    "2": "default"
  },
  "switches": [
    {
      "downlink_ips": [
        "10.255.240.6",
        "10.255.240.8"
      ],
      "downlinks": [
        "5c5b35000007",
        "5c5b35000008"
      ],
      "evpn_id": 1,
      "mac": "5c5b35000003",
      "model": "QFX10002-36Q",
      "role": "collapsed-core",
      "uplinks": [
        "5c5b35000005",
        "5c5b35000006"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Example response|[junos_evpn_topology](#schemajunos_evpn_topology)|

## upgradeOrgSsrs

<a id="opIdupgradeOrgSsrs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/ssr/upgrade \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "channel": "stable",
    "device_ids": [
      "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b3500001f",
      "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b35000020"
    ],
    "strategy": "big_bang",
    "version": "5.3.0-93"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/ssr/upgrade`

Upgrade Org SSRs

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "channel": "stable",
  "device_ids": [
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b3500001f",
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b35000020"
  ],
  "strategy": "big_bang",
  "version": "5.3.0-93"
}
```

<h3 id="upgradeorgssrs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» channel|body|string|false|upgrade channel to follow|
|» device_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|true|list of 128T device IDs to upgrade|
|» reboot_at|body|integer|false|reboot start time in epoch seconds, default is start_time, -1 disables reboot|
|» start_time|body|integer|false|128T firmware download start time in epoch seconds, default is now, -1 disables download|
|» strategy|body|string|false|* `big_bang`: upgrade all at once<br>* `serial`: one at a time|
|» version|body|string|false|128T firmware version to upgrade (e.g. 5.3.0-93)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» channel|stable|
|» channel|beta|
|» channel|alpha|
|» strategy|big_bang|
|» strategy|serial|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "channel": "stable",
  "counts": {
    "failed": 0,
    "queued": 1,
    "success": 0,
    "upgrading": 1
  },
  "device_type": "gateway",
  "id": "ceef2c8a-e2e6-447a-8b27-cb4f3ec1adae",
  "status": "upgrading",
  "strategy": "serial",
  "versions": {}
}
```

<h3 id="upgradeorgssrs-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Example response|[ssr_upgrade_response](#schemassr_upgrade_response)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

## getOrgGatewayTemplate

<a id="opIdgetOrgGatewayTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/gatewaytemplates/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

## getOrgInventory

<a id="opIdgetOrgInventory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/inventory \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/inventory`

Get Org Inventory

### VC (Virtual-Chassis) Management
Ideally VC should be managed as a single device - where - one managed entity where config / monitoring is anchored against (with a stable identify MAC) - all members appears in the inventory

In our implementation, we strive to achieve that without manual user configurations by 
1. during claim or adoption a VC, we require FPC0 to exist and will use its MAC as identify for the entire chassis
2. other VC members will be automatically populated when they’re all present

The perceivable result is 
1. from `/sites/:site_id/stats/devices/:fpc0_mac` API, you’d see the VC where module_stat contains the VC members 
2. from `/orgs/:org_id/inventory?vc=true` API, you’d see all VC members with vc_mac pointing to the FPC0

<h3 id="getorginventory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|query|string|false|device serial|
|model|query|string|false|device model|
|type|query|string|false|none|
|mac|query|string|false|MAC address|
|site_id|query|string|false|site id if assigned, null if not assigned|
|vc_mac|query|string|false|none|
|vc|query|string|false|none|
|unassigned|query|boolean|false|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|none|
|page|query|integer|false|none|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|ap|
|type|switch|
|type|gateway|
|type|mxedge|

## replaceOrgDevices

<a id="opIdreplaceOrgDevices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/inventory/replace \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "discard": [],
    "inventory_mac": "5c5b35000301",
    "mac": "5c5b35000101",
    "site_id": "4ac1dcf4-9d8b-7211-65c4-057819f0862b"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/inventory/replace`

It’s a common request we get from the customers. When a AP HW has problem and need a replacement, they would want to copy the existing attributes (Device Config) of this old AP to the new one. It can be done by providing the MAC of a device that’s currently in the inventory but not assigned. The Device replaced will become unassigned.

**Note:** For Gateway devices only like-for-like replacements (can only replace a SRX320 with a SRX320 and not some otehr model) are allowed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "discard": [],
  "inventory_mac": "5c5b35000301",
  "mac": "5c5b35000101",
  "site_id": "4ac1dcf4-9d8b-7211-65c4-057819f0862b"
}
```

<h3 id="replaceorgdevices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|Request Body|
|» discard|body|[string]|false|attributes that you don’t want to copy|
|» inventory_mac|body|string|true|mac of the inventory that will be replacing the old one. It has to be claimed and unassigned.|
|» mac|body|string|true|device mac|
|» site_id|body|string(uuid)|true|the site_id of the device to be replaced|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "error": [],
  "op": "assign",
  "success": [
    "5c5b350e0001"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="replaceorgdevices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<h3 id="replaceorgdevices-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|op|string|true|none|none|
|success|[string]|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|op|delete|
|op|assign|

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs-jsi">Orgs JSI</h1>

Juniper Support Insight is a free service provided to all Mist customers. You can adopt your devices via a few lines CLI comands. Allowing you to 
* get some basic information about the adopted devices 
* web shell into device (write privilege required) 
* upgrade (write privilege required)

## moveOrDeleteOrgLicenseToAnotherOrg

<a id="opIdmoveOrDeleteOrgLicenseToAnotherOrg"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/licenses \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "notes": "customer notes",
    "op": "annotate",
    "subscription_id": "SUB-000144"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/licenses`

Move, Undo Move or Delete Org License to Another Org
If the admin has admin privilege against the `org_id` and `dst_org_id`, he can move some of the licenses to another Org. Given that: 
1. the specified license is currently active 
2. there’s enough licenses left in the specified license (by subscription_id) 
3. there will still be enough entitled licenses for the type of license after the amendment

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "notes": "customer notes",
  "op": "annotate",
  "subscription_id": "SUB-000144"
}
```

<h3 id="moveordeleteorglicensetoanotherorg-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|Request Body|
|» amendment_id|body|string(uuid)|false|if `op`==`unamend`, the ID of the operation to cancel|
|» dst_org_id|body|string(uuid)|false|if `op`==`amend`, the id of the org where the licence is moved|
|» notes|body|string|false|if `op`==`annotate`|
|» op|body|string|true|to move a license, use the `amend` operation|
|» quantity|body|integer|false|if `op`==`amend`, the number of licences to mo|
|» subscription_id|body|string|false|if `op`==`amend`, the ID of the subscription to use|

#### Enumerated Values

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/maps/import`

Import data from files is a multipart POST which has an file, an optional json, and an optional csv, to create floorplan, assign matching inventory to specific site, place ap if name or mac matches

# CSV File Format
```csv
Vendor AP name,Mist AP Mac
US Office AP-2 - 5c:5b:35:00:00:02,5c5b35000002
```

```yaml
auto_deviceprofile_assignment: false
csv: string
file: string
json:
  import_all_floorpans: false
  import_height: true
  import_orientation: true
  site_id: "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  vendor_name: ekahau
```

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs-network-templates">Orgs Network Templates</h1>

Network template is intended to be applied to a Site. It works like a blueprint of the network of the site.
All Site Settings can go into Network Templates. See Site:Site Setting for schema
Moreover, this can be further be overwriten by individual Site Setting

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|[networktemplate](#schemanetworktemplate)|false|Request Body|

|» dns_suffix|body|[string]|false|none|
|» extra_routes|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|Property key is the destination CIDR or network name|
|» » » via|body|string|false|Next-hop address|

|» » » vlan_id|body|integer|false|none|
|» ntp_servers|body|[string]|false|none|
|» port_usages|body|object|false|The property key is the port profile name|

|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|

|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » internal_ip|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » port|body|string|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » restricted|body|boolean|false|by default, all access is allowed, to only allow certain traffic, make `restricted`=`true` and define service_policies|
|» » static_nat|body|object|false|The property key may be an IP Address (i.e. "172.16.0.1"), and IP Address and Port (i.e. "172.16.0.1:8443") or a CIDR (i.e. "172.16.0.12/20")|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|

|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» subnet|body|string|false|none|
|» tenants|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » addresses|body|string|false|none|
|» vlan_id|body|integer|false|none|
|» vpn_access|body|object|false|whether this network can be accessed from vpn|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » allow_ping|body|boolean|false|whether to allow ping from vpn into this routed network|
|» » » destination_nat|body|object|false|if `routed` = `false` (usually at Spoke), but some hosts needs to be reachable from Hub|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » » port|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » » to|body|string|false|none|
|» » » nat_pool|body|string|false|if `routed` = `false` (usually at Spoke), but some hosts needs to be reachable from Hub|

|» » » source_nat|body|object|false|if `routed`==`false` (usually at Spoke), but some hosts needs to be reachable from Hub|
|» » » » exteral_ip|body|string|false|when `nat_pool` is used with {{VARS}} in bigger deployments with lots of spokes for source_nat and static_nat to work, we need the summarized subnet to set up Hub's policy correctly|
|» » » static_nat|body|object|false|if `routed` = `false` (usually at Spoke), but some hosts needs to be reachable from Hub|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » » » » to|body|string|false|none|
|» » » summarized_nat_pool|body|string|false|none|

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs-psk-portals">Orgs Psk Portals</h1>

PSK Self-Service Portals are for 
  1. **WIFI users** who want to connect to a WLAN with personal PSK, they’re told to connect to a URL where they can login (likely through company’s SSO) and get the WIFI Name / Passphrase - required input fields name, email so we can generate PSK 
  2. **PSK Admins** (they don’t have access to normal Network Admin Portal)
When a PSK portal is created, an unique URL will be generated (e.g. https://psk.mist.com/xxxxxx)

## getOrgPskPortals

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

2. **PSK Admins** (they don’t have access to normal Network Admin Portal)

<h1 id="mist-api-orgs-secpolicies">Orgs SecPolicies</h1>

Security Policy is designed to audit / catch discripancies between “what’s intended to be running” versus “what’s actually running” in a network. Many big organizations have separated Security and IT team (for good reasons). Each site can be assigned a security policy. Whenever an AP is provisioned, the configuration will be checked against the security policy. Any violations will be flagged in [Device Config History](#tag/Sites-Devices/operation/searchSiteDeviceConfigHistory) where you can search for the when and where the violation occurs.

Create getOrgServices Service

```json
  "specs": [

    }
  ],

}
```

<h3 id="createorgservice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[service](#schemaservice)|false|none|
|» addresses|body|[string]|false|if `type`==`custom`, the subnets where the service resides (if more specific is required)|
|» app_caetgories|body|[string]|false|list of application categories are available through /api/v1/const/app_categories|
|» apps|body|[string]|false|when `type`==`app`, comes from `/api/v1/const/apps`<br>when `type`==`app_categories`, comes from `/api/v1/const/app_categories`|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» dscp|body|integer|false|when `traffic_type`==`custom`|
|» failover_policy|body|string|false|none|
|» hostnames|body|[string]|false|if `type`==`custom`|
|» id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» max_jitter|body|integer|false|when `traffic_type`==`custom`, for uplink selection|
|» max_latency|body|string|false|when `traffic_type`==`custom`, for uplink selection|
|» max_loss|body|integer|false|when `traffic_type`==`custom`, for uplink selection|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» sle_enabled|body|boolean|false|whether to enable measure SLE|
|» specs|body|[object]|false|when `type`==`addresses` or `type`==`hostnames`|
|» » port_range|body|integer|false|none|
|» » protocol|body|string|false|`https`/ `tcp` / `udp` / `icmp` / `gre` / `any` / `:protocol_number`.<br>`protocol_number` is between 1-254|
|» traffic_class|body|string|false|when `traffic_type`==`custom`|
|» traffic_type|body|string|false|values from `/api/v1/consts/traffic_types`<br>* when `type`==`apps`, we'll choose traffic_type automatically<br>* when `type`==`addresses` or `type`==`hostnames`, you can provide your own settings (optional)|
|» type|body|string|false|none|
|» vpn_name|body|string|false|none|

|» type|app|
|» type|app_categories|

|» vpn_name|local|
|» vpn_name|hostname|

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/setting/pcap_bucket/setup`

Provide Customer Bucket Name

Setting up Custom PCAP Bucket Involves the following:
* provide the bucket name
* we’ll attempt to write a file MIST_TOKEN
* you have to verify the ownership of the bucket by providing the content of the MIST_TOKEN

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bucket": "company-private-pcap"
}
```

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/sites/{site_name}/maps/import`

Import data from files is a multipart POST which has an file, an optional json, and an optional csv, to create floorplan, assign matching inventory to specific site, place ap if name or mac matches

#### Request

```
"json": a JSON string describing your upload
"file": a binary file
```

> Body parameter

```yaml
csl: string
file: string
```

<h3 id="importorgmaptosite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|site_name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|a JSON string, site id required, vendor option: ekahau, ibwave, etc., import_all_floorplans: optional, default: false, import_height: optional, default: true, import_orientation: optional, default: true<br>"file": a binary file, option: .esx<br>"csv": a csv file for ap name mapping, optional|
|» csl|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|false|none|

```json
    "num_ap_assigned": 1,
    "num_inv_assigned": 1,
    "num_map_assigned": 1
  }
}
```

<h3 id="createorgsso-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[sso](#schemasso)|false|Request Body|
|» custom_logout_url|body|string|false|optional, a URL we will redirect the user after user logout from Mist (for some IdP which supports a custom logout URL that is different from SP-initiated SLO process)|
|» default_role|body|string|false|default role to assign if there’s no match. By default, an assertion is treated as invalid when there’s no role matched|

|» idp_cert|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`saml`. IDP Cert (used to verify the signed response)|
|» idp_sign_algo|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`saml`. Signing algorithm for SAML Assertion|
|» idp_sso_url|body|string|false|IDP Single-Sign-On URL|
|» idp_type|body|string|false|none|
|» ignore_unmatched_roles|body|boolean|false|ignore any unmatched roles provided in assertion. By default, an assertion is treated as invalid for any unmatched role|
|» issuer|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`saml`. IDP issuer URL|
|» ldap_base_dn|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_bind_dn|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_bind_password|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_certs|body|[string]|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_client_cert|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_client_key|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_group_attr|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_group_dn|body|string|false|if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|» ldap_group_filter|body|string|false|if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|» ldap_server_hosts|body|[string]|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_type|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|» ldap_user_filter|body|string|false|* if `ldap_type`==`ad`: "(CN=%s)"<br>* if `ldap_type`==`okta`: "(uid=%s)"<br>* if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|» name|body|string|true|name|
|» nameid_format|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`saml`|
|» oauth_cc_client_id|body|string|false|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, Client Credentials|
|» oauth_cc_client_secret|body|string|false|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, oauth_cc_client_secret is RSA private key, of the form "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY--...."|
|» oauth_discovery_url|body|string|false|if `idp_type`==`oauth`|

|» oauth_ropc_secret|body|string|false|oauth_ropc_client_secret can be empty if oauth_type is azure|
|» oauth_tenant_id|body|string|false|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, oauth_tenant_id|
|» oauth_type|body|string|false|none|
|» role_attr_extraction|body|string|false|optional, custom role attribute parsing scheme<br><br>Supported Role Parsing Schemes<br><table><tr><th>Name</th><th>Scheme</th></tr><tr><td>cn</td><td><ul><li>The expected role attribute format in SAML Assertion is “CN=cn,OU=ou1,OU=ou2,…”</li><li>CN (the key) is case insensitive and exactly 1 CN is expected (or the entire entry will be ignored)</li><li>E.g. if role attribute is “CN=cn,OU=ou1,OU=ou2” then parsed role value is “cn”</li></ul></td></tr></table>|

## getOrgDevicesStats

<a id="opIdgetOrgDevicesStats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/orgs/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/stats/devices \

  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/stats/devices`

Org Devices stats
This API renders some high-level device stats, pagination is assumed and returned in response header (as the response is an array)


<h3 id="getorgdevicesstats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|none|
|start|query|integer|false|none|
|end|query|integer|false|none|
|duration|query|string|false|For historical stats and/or logs where time range is needed, you can specify the time range in a few different ways:<br>  * ?start=1430000000&end=1430864000	specify the start / end<br>  * ?end=1430864000&duration=1d	specify end time and duration<br>  * ?duration=1d	specify duration, end will be now() in seconds|
|type|query|string|false|none|
|status|query|string|false|none|
|site_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|mac|query|string|false|none|
|evpntopo_id|query|string(uuid)|false|EVPN Topology ID|
|evpn_unused|query|string|false|if `evpn_unused`==`true`, find EVPN eligible switches which don’t belong to any EVPN Topology yet|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|ap|
|type|switch|
|type|gateways|
|type|all|
|status|all|
|status|connected|
|status|disconnected|

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/webhooks`

Create Org Webhook

**N.B**. For org webhooks, only device-events/alarms/audits/client-join/client-sessions/device-updowns/mxedge-events Infrastructure topics are supported.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "headers": {},
  "name": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "splunk_token": "string",
  "topics": [],
  "type": "http-post",
  "url": "string",
  "verify_cert": false
}
```

|» enabled|body|boolean|false|whether webhook is enabled|
|» headers|body|object \| null|false|custom headers : the headers name and value must be string, total bytes of headers name and value must be less than 1000|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|name of the webhook|
|» secret|body|string \| null|false|only if `type`=`http-post`<br>when `secret` is provided, two HTTP headers will be added:<br>  * X-Mist-Signature-v2: HMAC_SHA256(secret, body)<br>  * X-Mist-Signature: HMAC_SHA1(secret, body)|
|» splunk_token|body|string \| null|false|splunk token (If splunk_token is not defined for a type Splunk webhook, it will not send, regardless if the webhook receiver is configured to accept it.)|
|» topics|body|[string]|false|N.B. For org webhooks, only device-events/alarms/audits/client-join/client-sessions/nac-sessions topics are supported.|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|http-post (default) / splunk / google-pubsub / aws-sns|
|» url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» verify_cert|body|boolean|false|when url uses HTTPS, whether to verify the certificate|

`PUT /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/webhooks/{webhook_id}`

Update Org Webhook

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "headers": {},
  "name": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "splunk_token": "string",
  "topics": [],
  "type": "http-post",
  "url": "string",
  "verify_cert": false
}
```

<h3 id="updateorgwebhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|webhook_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[webhook](#schemawebhook)|false|Request Body|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|whether webhook is enabled|
|» headers|body|object \| null|false|custom headers : the headers name and value must be string, total bytes of headers name and value must be less than 1000|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|name of the webhook|
|» secret|body|string \| null|false|only if `type`=`http-post`<br>when `secret` is provided, two HTTP headers will be added:<br>  * X-Mist-Signature-v2: HMAC_SHA256(secret, body)<br>  * X-Mist-Signature: HMAC_SHA1(secret, body)|
|» splunk_token|body|string \| null|false|splunk token (If splunk_token is not defined for a type Splunk webhook, it will not send, regardless if the webhook receiver is configured to accept it.)|
|» topics|body|[string]|false|N.B. For org webhooks, only device-events/alarms/audits/client-join/client-sessions/nac-sessions topics are supported.|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|http-post (default) / splunk / google-pubsub / aws-sns|
|» url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» verify_cert|body|boolean|false|when url uses HTTPS, whether to verify the certificate|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» topics|alarms|
|» topics|asset-raw|
|» topics|asset-raw-rssi|
|» topics|audits|
|» topics|client-join|
|» topics|client-sessions|
|» topics|device-events|
|» topics|device-updowns|
|» topics|discovered-raw-rssi|
|» topics|location|
|» topics|mxedge-events|
|» topics|nac-sessions|
|» topics|occupancy-alerts|
|» topics|rssizone|
|» topics|sdkclient-scan-data|
|» topics|vbeacon|
|» topics|wifi-conn-raw|
|» topics|wifi-unconn-raw|
|» topics|zone|
|» type|http-post|
|» type|splunk|

```json
  "enabled": true,
  "headers": {},
  "id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "modified_time": 0,
  "name": "string",
```

<h3 id="createorgwlan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[wlan](#schemawlan)|false|Request Body|
|» acct_interim_interval|body|integer|false|how frequently should interim accounting be reported, 60-65535. default is 0 (use one specified in Access-Accept request from RADIUS Server). Very frequent messages can affect the performance of the radius server, 600 and up is recommended when enabled|
|» acct_servers|body|[[acct_server](#schemaacct_server)]|false|list of RADIUS accounting servers, optional, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|» airwatch|body|[wlan_airwatch](#schemawlan_airwatch)|false|airwatch wlan settings|
|» allow_ipv6_ndp|body|boolean|false|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows or disallows ipv6 Neighbor Discovery packets to go through|
|» allow_mdns|body|boolean|false|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows mDNS / Bonjour packets to go through|
|» allow_ssdp|body|boolean|false|only applicable when `limit_bcast`==`tru`e, which allows SSDP|
|» ap_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|list of device ids|
|» app_limit|body|object|false|bandwidth limiting for apps (applies to up/down)|
|» » apps|body|object|false|map from app key to bandwidth in kbps. app key defined in Get Application List|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » wxtag_ids|body|object|false|map from wxtag_id of Hostname Wxlan Tags to bandwidth in kbps|
|» app_qos|body|[wlan_app_qos](#schemawlan_app_qos)|false|app qos wlan settings|
|» apply_to|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» arp_filter|body|boolean|false|whether to enable smart arp filter|
|» auth|body|[wlan_auth](#schemawlan_auth)|false|authentication wlan settings|
|» auth_server_selection|body|string \| null|false|When ordered, AP will prefer and go back to the first server if possible|
|» auth_servers|body|[[auth_server](#schemaauth_server)]|false|list of RADIUS authentication servers, at least one is needed if `auth type`==`eap`, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|» auth_servers_nas_id|body|string \| null|false|optional, up to 48 bytes, will be dynamically generated if not provided. used only for authentication servers|
|» auth_servers_nas_ip|body|string \| null|false|optional, NAS-IP-ADDRESS to use|
|» auth_servers_retries|body|integer|false|radius auth session retries|
|» auth_servers_timeout|body|integer|false|radius auth session timeout|
|» band|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** `band` is deprecated and kept for backward compability. Use bands instead|
|» band_steer|body|boolean|false|whether to enable band_steering, this works only when band==both|
|» band_steer_force_band5|body|boolean|false|force dual-band capable client to connect to 5G|
|» bands|body|[string]|false|list of radios that the wlan should apply to|
|» block_blacklist_clients|body|boolean|false|whether to block the clients in the blacklist (up to first 256 macs)|
|» bonjour|body|[wlan_bonjour](#schemawlan_bonjour)|false|bonjour gateway wlan settings|
|» cisco_cwa|body|[wlan_cisco_cwa](#schemawlan_cisco_cwa)|false|Cisco CWA (central web authentication) required RADIUS with COA in order to work. See CWA: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/security/identity-services-engine/115732-central-web-auth-00.html<br>|
|» client_limit_down|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» client_limit_down_enabled|body|boolean|false|if downlink limiting per-client is enabled|
|» client_limit_up|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» client_limit_up_enabled|body|boolean|false|if uplink limiting per-client is enabled|
|» coa_servers|body|[[coa_server](#schemacoa_server)]|false|list of COA (change of authorization) servers, optional|
|» disable_11ax|body|boolean|false|some old WLAN drivers may not be compatible|
|» disable_ht_vht_rates|body|boolean|false|to disable ht or vht rates|
|» disable_uapsd|body|boolean|false|whether to disable U-APSD|
|» disable_v1_roam_notify|body|boolean|false|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|» disable_v2_roam_notify|body|boolean|false|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|» disable_wmm|body|boolean|false|whether to disable WMM|
|» dns_server_rewrite|body|object \| null|false|for radius_group-based DNS server (rewrite DNS request depending on the Group RADIUS server returns)|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » radius_groups|body|object|false|map between radius_group and the desired DNS server (IPv4 only)|
|» dtim|body|integer|false|none|
|» dynamic_psk|body|object \| null|false|for dynamic PSK where we get per-user PSK from Radius<br>dynamic_psk allows PSK to be selected at runtime depending on context (wlan/site/user/...) thus following configurations are assumed (currently)<br>- PSK will come from RADIUS server<br>- AP sends client MAC as username ans password (i.e. `enable_mac_auth` is assumed)<br>- AP sends BSSID:SSID as Caller-Station-ID<br>- `auth_servers` is required<br>- PSK will come from cloud WLC if source is cloud_psks<br>- default_psk will be used if cloud WLC is not available<br>- `multi_psk_only` and `psk` is ignored<br>- `pairwise` can only be wpa2-ccmp (for now, wpa3 support on the roadmap)|
|» » default_psk|body|string|false|default PSK to use if cloud WLC is not available, 8-63 characters|
|» » default_vlan_id|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » source|body|string|false|none|
|» » vlan_ids|body|[integer \| null]|false|none|
|» dynamic_vlan|body|object \| null|false|for 802.1x|
|» » default_vlan_id|body|integer \| null|false|vlan_id to use when there’s no match from RADIUS|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether to enable dynamic vlan|
|» » local_vlan_ids|body|[integer \| null]|false|vlan_ids to be locally bridged|
|» » type|body|string \| null|false|standard (using Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, widely supported), airespace-interface-name (Airespace/Cisco)|
|» » vlans|body|object|false|map between vlan_id (as string) to airespace interface names (comma-separated) or null for stndard mapping|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» enable_local_keycaching|body|boolean|false|enable AP-AP keycaching via multicast|
|» enable_wireless_bridging|body|boolean|false|whether to enable wireless bridging, which allows more broadcast packets to go through<br>(allows forwarding of DHCP response to client not associated with the AP)|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|if this wlan is enabled|
|» hide_ssid|body|boolean|false|whether to hide SSID in beacon|
|» hostname_ie|body|boolean|false|include hostname inside IE in AP beacons / probe responses|
|» hotspot20|body|[wlan_hotspot_20](#schemawlan_hotspot_20)|false|hostspot 2.0 wlan settings|
|» interface|body|string|false|where this WLAN will be connected to|
|» isolation|body|boolean|false|whether to allow clients to talk to each other|
|» l2_isolation|body|boolean|false|if isolation is enabled, whether to deny clients to talk to L2 on the LAN|
|» legacy_overds|body|boolean|false|legacy devices requires the Over-DS (for Fast BSS Transition) bit set (while our chip doesn’t support it). Warning! Enabling this will cause problem for iOS devices.|
|» limit_bcast|body|boolean|false|whether to limit broadcast packets going to wireless (i.e. only allow certain bcast packets to go through)|
|» limit_probe_response|body|boolean|false|limit probe response base on some heuristic rules|
|» max_idletime|body|integer|false|max idle time in seconds|
|» mist_nac|body|object|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|when enabled:<br>* `auth_servers` is ignored<br>* `acct_servers` is ignored<br>* `auth_servers_*` are ignored<br>* `coa_servers` is ignored<br>* `radsec` is ignored|
|» mxtunnel|body|object|false|when `interface`=`site_medge`, the definition of the Mist Tunnels (key is the name)|
|» mxtunnel_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|when `interface`=`mxtunnel`, id of the Mist Tunnel|
|» mxtunnel_name|body|string \| null|false|when `interface`=`site_medge`, name of the mxtunnel that in mxtunnels under Site Setting|
|» no_static_dns|body|boolean|false|whether to only allow client to use DNS that we’ve learned from DHCP response|
|» no_static_ip|body|boolean|false|whether to only allow client that we’ve learned from DHCP exchange to talk|
|» portal|body|[wlan_portal](#schemawlan_portal)|false|portal wlan settings|
|» portal_allowed_hostnames|body|[string]|false|list of hostnames without http(s):// (matched by substring)|
|» portal_allowed_subnets|body|[string]|false|list of CIDRs|
|» portal_api_secret|body|string \| null|false|api secret (auto-generated) that can be used to sign guest authorization requests|
|» portal_denied_hostnames|body|[string]|false|list of hostnames without http(s):// (matched by substring), this takes precedence over portal_allowed_hostnames|
|» portal_image|body|string(uri) \| null|false|Url of portal background image|
|» portal_sso_url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» portal_template_url|body|string \| null|false|N.B portal_template will be forked out of wlan objects soon. To fetch portal_template, please query portal_template_url. To update portal_template, use Wlan Portal Template.|
|» qos|body|object|false|none|
|» » class|body|string|false|none|
|» » overwrite|body|boolean|false|whether to overwrite QoS|
|» radsec|body|[radsec](#schemaradsec)|false|Radsec settings|

|» » 5|body|[wlan_datarates](#schemawlan_datarates)|false|data rates wlan settings|

Create Org WxAN Tunnel

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dmvpn": {
    "enabled": false,
    "holding_time": 0,
    "host_routes": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "for_mgmt": false,
  "hello_interval": 60,
  "hello_retries": 7,
  "hostname": "string",
  "ipsec": {
    "enabled": false,

  },

  "mtu": 0,

  ],

  "sessions": [
    {
      "ap_as_session_id": "string",
      "comment": "string",
      "enable_cookie": true,
      "ethertype": "ethernet",
      "local_session_id": 1,
      "pseudo_802.1ad_enabled": false,
      "remote_id": "string",
      "remote_session_id": 1,
      "use_ap_as_session_ids": false
    }
  ],
  "udp_port": 0,
  "use_udp": false
}
```

<h3 id="createorgwxtunnel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[wxlan_tunnel](#schemawxlan_tunnel)|false|Request Body|
|» dmvpn|body|object|false|Dynamic Multipoint VPN configurations|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether DMVPN is enabled|
|» » holding_time|body|integer|false|optional; the holding time for NHRP ‘registration requests’ and ‘resolution replies’ sent from the Mist AP (in seconds); default 600|
|» » host_routes|body|[string]|false|optional; list of IPv4 DMVPN peer host ip-addresses to which traffic is forwarded|
|» for_mgmt|body|boolean|false|determined during creation time and cannot be toggled. A management tunnel cannot be used by wxlan rule or by wlan|
|» hello_interval|body|integer|false|in seconds, used as heartbeat to detect if a tunnel is alive. AP will try another peer after missing N hellos specified by hello_retries.|
|» hello_retries|body|integer|false|none|
|» hostname|body|string|false|optional, overwrite the hostname in SCCRQ control message, default is “” or null, %H and %M can be used, which will be replace with corresponding values:<br>* %H: name of the ap if provided (and will be stripped so it can be used for hostname) and fallbacks to MAC<br>* %M: MAC (e.g. 5c5b350e0060)|
|» ipsec|body|object|false|IPSec-related configurations; requires DMVPN be enabled|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether ipsec is enabled, requires DMVPN be enabled|
|» » psk|body|string|true|ipsec pre-shared key|
|» is_static|body|boolean|false|whether it’s static/unmanaged (i.e. no control session). As the session configurations are not compatible, cannot be toggled.|
|» mtu|body|integer|false|0 to enable PMTU, 552-1500 to start PMTU with a lower MTU|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the tunnel|
|» org_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» peers|body|[string]|false|list of remote peers’ IP or hostname|
|» router_id|body|string|false|optional, overwrite the router-id in SCCRQ control message, default is “0” or null, can also be an IPv4 address|
|» secret|body|string|false|secret, ‘’ if no auth is used|
|» sessions|body|[object]|false|sessions to be established with the tunnel. Has to be >= 1 in order for this tunnel to be useful. For management tunnel, it can only have 1|
|» » ap_as_session_id|body|string|false|if `use_ap_as_session_ids`==`true`, only apmac is supported right now. This is the name WLAN should use for wxtunnel_remote_id|
|» » comment|body|string|false|optional, user-specified string for display purpose|
|» » enable_cookie|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » ethertype|body|string|false|none|
|» » local_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » pseudo_802.1ad_enabled|body|boolean|false|optional. Enables the pseudo 802.1ad QinQ mode where the AP device drops the outer vlan tag (QinQ). This mode is useful when tunneling Mist AP’s to some aggregation routers.|
|» » remote_id|body|string|false|remote-id of the session, has to be unique in the same tunnel|
|» » remote_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » use_ap_as_session_ids|body|boolean|false|whether to use AP (last 4 bytes of MAC currently) as session ids|
|» udp_port|body|integer|false|udp port if `use_udp`==`true`|
|» use_udp|body|boolean|false|whether to use UDP instead of IP (proto=115, which is default of L2TPv3)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » ethertype|ethernet|
|» » ethertype|vlan|

|» sessions|body|[object]|false|sessions to be established with the tunnel. Has to be >= 1 in order for this tunnel to be useful. For management tunnel, it can only have 1|
|» » ap_as_session_id|body|string|false|if `use_ap_as_session_ids`==`true`, only apmac is supported right now. This is the name WLAN should use for wxtunnel_remote_id|
|» » comment|body|string|false|optional, user-specified string for display purpose|
|» » enable_cookie|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » ethertype|body|string|false|none|
|» » local_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » pseudo_802.1ad_enabled|body|boolean|false|optional. Enables the pseudo 802.1ad QinQ mode where the AP device drops the outer vlan tag (QinQ). This mode is useful when tunneling Mist AP’s to some aggregation routers.|
|» » remote_id|body|string|false|remote-id of the session, has to be unique in the same tunnel|
|» » remote_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » use_ap_as_session_ids|body|boolean|false|whether to use AP (last 4 bytes of MAC currently) as session ids|
|» udp_port|body|integer|false|udp port if `use_udp`==`true`|
|» use_udp|body|boolean|false|whether to use UDP instead of IP (proto=115, which is default of L2TPv3)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » ethertype|ethernet|
|» » ethertype|vlan|

<h1 id="mist-api-sites">Sites</h1>

<h3 id="createsitebeacon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[beacon](#schemabeacon)|false|Request Body|
|» eddystone_instance|body|string|false|Eddystone-UID instance (6 bytes) in hexstring format|
|» eddystone_namespace|body|string|false|Eddystone-UID namespace (10 bytes) in hexstring format|
|» eddystone_url|body|string|false|Eddystone-URL url|
|» ibeacon_major|body|integer|false|bluetooth tag major|
|» ibeacon_minor|body|integer|false|bluetooth tag minor|
|» ibeacon_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|bluetooth tag UUID|
|» mac|body|string|false|optiona, MAC of the beacon, currently used only to identify battery voltage|
|» map_id|body|string(uuid)|false|map where the device belongs to|

<h1 id="mist-api-sites-devices">Sites Devices</h1>

Mist provides many ways (device-type specific template, site template, device profile, per-device) to configure devices for different kind of scenarios.
The precedence goes from most specific to least specific
Device > Device Profile > RFTemplate (for AP only) > DeviceType-specific Template > Site Template > Site Setting

|start|query|integer|false|none|
|end|query|integer|false|none|
|duration|query|string|false|For historical stats and/or logs where time range is needed, you can specify the time range in a few different ways:<br>  * ?start=1430000000&end=1430864000	specify the start / end<br>  * ?end=1430864000&duration=1d	specify end time and duration<br>  * ?duration=1d	specify duration, end will be now() in seconds|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

```json
  ],

  "total": 0
```

## searchSiteDevicesEvents

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/events/search`

Search Devices Events

<h3 id="searchsitedevicesevents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|device_type|query|string|false|none|
|mac|query|string|false|device mac|
|model|query|string|false|device model|
|text|query|string|false|event message|
|timestamp|query|string|false|event time|
|type|query|string|false|see [Event Types Definition](/#tag/Constants/operation/getDeviceEventsDefinitions)|
|limit|query|integer|false|none|
|start|query|integer|false|none|
|end|query|integer|false|none|
|duration|query|string|false|For historical stats and/or logs where time range is needed, you can specify the time range in a few different ways:<br>  * ?start=1430000000&end=1430864000	specify the start / end<br>  * ?end=1430864000&duration=1d	specify end time and duration<br>  * ?duration=1d	specify duration, end will be now() in seconds|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|device_type|ap|
|device_type|switch|
|device_type|gateway|

```json
  "results": [
    {
      "last_reboot_time": 1531854327,

    },
    {
      "timestamp": 1531854326,
      "type": "AP_CONFIGURED"
    }
  ],
  "start": 1531776183,
  "total": 14
}
```
