## countSiteDeviceLastConfig

<a id="opIdcountSiteDeviceLastConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/last_config/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/last_config/count`

Counts the number of entries in device config history for distinct field with given filters

<h3 id="countsitedevicelastconfig-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|distinct|query|string|false|none|
|page|query|integer|false|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|none|
|start|query|integer|false|none|
|end|query|integer|false|none|
|duration|query|string|false|For historical stats and/or logs where time range is needed, you can specify the time range in a few different ways:<br>  * ?start=1430000000&end=1430864000	specify the start / end<br>  * ?end=1430864000&duration=1d	specify end time and duration<br>  * ?duration=1d	specify duration, end will be now() in seconds|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|distinct|version|
|distinct|name|
|distinct|site_id|
|distinct|mac|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "distinct": "ap",
  "end": 1604310805,
  "limit": 10,
  "percentage": 100,
  "results": [
    {
      "ap": "5c5b35000000",
      "count": 1
    },
    {
      "ap": "5c5b35000001",
      "count": 1
    }
  ],
  "start": 1604307205,
  "total": 2
}
```

|200|OK|OK|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|end|integer|true|none|none|
|limit|integer|true|none|none|
|percentage|integer|true|none|none|
|results|[object]|true|none|none|

|» count|integer|true|none|none|

```json
    ]
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/restart`

Note that only the devices that are connected will be restarted.

```json
  "device_ids": [
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b35584a6f",
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b350ea3b3"
  ]
}
```

## multiUpgradeSiteDevices

<a id="opIdmultiUpgradeSiteDevices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/upgrade \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "canary_phases": [
      1,
      10,
      50,
      100
    ],
    "device_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "enable_p2p": true,
    "force": false,
    "max_failure_percentage": 5,
    "max_failures": [
      0
    ],
    "models": [
      "string"
    ],
    "start_time": 0,
    "strategy": "big_bang",
    "version": "stable"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/upgrade`

Upgrade Multiple Device

**Note**: this call doesn’t guarantee the devices to be upgraded right away (they may be offline)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "canary_phases": [
    1,
    10,
    50,
    100
  ],
  "device_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "enable_p2p": true,
  "force": false,
  "max_failure_percentage": 5,
  "max_failures": [
    0
  ],
  "models": [
    "string"
  ],
  "start_time": 0,
  "strategy": "big_bang",
  "version": "stable"
}
```

<h3 id="multiupgradesitedevices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[device_upgrade](#schemadevice_upgrade)|false|Request Body|
|» canary_phases|body|[integer]|false|phases for canary deployment. Each phase represents percentage of AP’s that need to be upgraded. default is [1, 10, 50, 100]|
|» device_ids|body|[string]|false|none|
|» enable_p2p|body|boolean|false|whether to allow local AP-to-AP FW upgrade|
|» force|body|boolean|false|true will force upgrade when requested version is same as running version|
|» max_failure_percentage|body|number|false|percentage of failures allowed across the entire upgrade(not applicable for `big_bang`)|
|» max_failures|body|[integer]|false|number of failures allowed within each phase(applicable for `canary` or `rrm`). Will be used if provided, else max_failure_percentage will be used|
|» models|body|[string]|false|none|
|» p2p_cluster_size|body|integer|false|none|
|» p2p_parallelism|body|integer|false|number of parallel p2p download batches to creat|
|» reboot|body|boolean|false|Reboot device immediately after upgrade is completed (Available on Junos OS devices)|
|» reboot_at|body|number|false|reboot start time in epoch seconds, default is `start_time`|
|» rrm_first_batch_percentage|body|integer|false|percentage of AP’s that need to be present in the first rrm batch|
|» rrm_max_batch_percentage|body|integer|false|max percentage of AP’s that need to be present in each rrm batch|
|» rrm_mesh_upgrade|body|string|false|sequential or parallel (default parallel). Whether to upgrade mesh AP’s parallelly or sequentially at the end of the upgrade|
|» rrm_node_order|body|string|false|Used in rrm to determine whether to start upgrade from fringe or center AP’s|
|» rrm_slow_ramp|body|boolean|false|true will make rrm batch sizes slowly ramp up|
|» snapshot|body|boolean|false|Perform recovery snapshot after device is rebooted (Available on Junos OS devices)|
|» start_time|body|number|false|upgrade start time in epoch seconds, default is now|
|» strategy|body|string|false|`big_bang` (upgrade all at once), `serial` (one at a time), `canary` or `rrm`|
|» version|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» rrm_node_order|fringe_to_center|
|» rrm_node_order|center_to_fringe|
|» strategy|big_bang|
|» strategy|canary|
|» strategy|serial|
|» strategy|rrm|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "counts": {
    "downloaded": 0,
    "failed": 0,
    "reboot_in_progress": 0,
    "rebooted": 0,
    "total": 0
  },
  "enable_p2p": true,
  "force": true,
  "id": "473f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f18",
  "start_time": 0,
  "status": "created",
  "strategy": "big_bang",
  "target_version": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="multiupgradesitedevices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[device_upgrade_response](#schemadevice_upgrade_response)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

<h3 id="updatesitedevice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[device_ap](#schemadevice_ap) \| [device_switch](#schemadevice_switch) \| [device_gateway](#schemadevice_gateway)|false|Request Body|
|» *oneOf*|body|[device_ap](#schemadevice_ap)|false|AP|
|» *oneOf*|body|[device_switch](#schemadevice_switch)|false|Switch Configuration<br>You can configure `port_usages` and `networks` settings at the device level, but most of the time it's better use the Site Setting to achieve better consistency and be able to re-use the same settings across switches entries defined here will "replace" those defined in Site Setting/Network Template|
|» *oneOf*|body|[device_gateway](#schemadevice_gateway)|false|device gateway|

## getSiteDeviceConfigCmd

<a id="opIdgetSiteDeviceConfigCmd"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/config_cmd \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/config_cmd`

Get Config CLI Commands
For a brown-field switch deployment where we adopted the switch through Adoption Command, we do not wipe out / overwrite the existing config automatically. Instead, we generate CLI commands that we would have generated. The user can inspect, modify, and incorporate this into their existing config manually.

Once they feel comfortable about the config we generate, they can enable allow_mist_config where we will take full control of their config like a claimed switch

<h3 id="getsitedeviceconfigcmd-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort|query|string|false|Make output cmds sorted (for better readability) or not.|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|true|
|sort|false|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "cli": [
    "set system hostname corp-a135"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="getsitedeviceconfigcmd-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<h3 id="getsitedeviceconfigcmd-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cli|[string]|true|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

## uploadSiteDeviceSupportFile

<a id="opIduploadSiteDeviceSupportFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/support \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "info": "full"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/support`

Support / Upload device support files

#### Info Param
**Parameter**|**Type**|**Description** 
 :-------------: |:-------------: |:-------------: 
process|string|Upload 1 file with output of show system processes extensive
outbound-ssh|string|Upload 1 file that concatenates all /var/log/outbound-ssh.log* files
messages|string|Upload 1 to 10 /var/log/messages* files
core-dumps|string|Upload all core dump files, if any
full|string|Upload 1 file with output of request support information, 1 file that concatenates all /var/log/outbound-ssh.log files, all core dump files, and the 3 most recent /var/log/messages files

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "info": "full"
}
```

<h3 id="uploadsitedevicesupportfile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|Request Body|
|» info|body|string|false|optional choice: process, outbound-ssh, and full (default)|
|» node|body|string|false|optional: for SSR, if node is not present, both nodes support files are uploaded|
|» num_messages_files|body|integer|false|optional: number of most recent messages files to upload.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» info|process|
|» info|outbound-ssh|
|» info|full|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

## portsBounceFromSwitch

<a id="opIdportsBounceFromSwitch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/bounce_port \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "ports": [
      "ge-0/0/0",
      "ge-0/0/1"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/bounce_port`

Port Bounce can be performed from the Switch.The output will be available through websocket. As there can be multiple command issued against the same AP at the same time and the output all goes through the same websocket stream, session is introduced for demux.

#### Subscribe to Device Command outputs
`WS /api-ws/v1/stream`

```json
{
    "subscribe": "/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/cmd"
}
```
##### Example output from ws stream
```json
{
    "event": "data",
    "channel": "/sites/4ac1dcf4-9d8b-7211-65c4-057819f0862b/devices/00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b350e0060/cmd",
    "data": {
        "session": "session_id",
        "raw": "Port bounce complete."
    }
}
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ports": [
    "ge-0/0/0",
    "ge-0/0/1"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="portsbouncefromswitch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|Request Body|
|» port|body|string|false|the port to bounce|
|» ports|body|[string]|false|list of ports to bounce|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="portsbouncefromswitch-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

```json
        "raw": "Interface TDR detail:\nTest status : Test successfully executed  ge-0/0/0\n"

}

}
```

## createSiteEvpnTopology

<a id="opIdcreateSiteEvpnTopology"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/evpn_topologies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "CC",
    "overwrite": true,
    "pod_names": {
      "1": "default",
      "2": "default"
    },
    "switches": [
      {
        "mac": "5c5b35000003",
        "role": "collapsed-core"
      },
      {
        "mac": "5c5b35000004",
        "role": "collapsed-core"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/evpn_topologies`

While all the `evpn_id` / `downlink_ips` can be specifidd by hand, the easiest way is to call the `build_vpn_topology` API, allowing you to examine the diff, and update it yourself. You can also simply call it with `overwrite=true` which will apply the updates for you.

**Notes:**
1. You can use `core` / `distribution` / `access` to create a CLOS topology
2. You can also use `core` / `distribution` to form a 2-tier EVPN topology where ESI-Lag is configured distribution to connect to access switches
3. In a small/medium campus, `collapsed-core` can be used where core switches are the inter-connected to do EVPN
4. The API uses a few pre-defined parameters and best-practices to generate the configs. It can be customized by using `evpn_options` in Site Setting / Network Template. (e.g. a different subnet for the underlay)

#### Collapsed Core
In a small-medium campus, EVPN can also be enabled only at the core switches (up to 4) by assigning all participating switches with `collapsed-core role`. When there are more than 2 switches, a ring-like topology will be formed.

#### ESI-Lag
If the access switchess does not have EVPN support, you can take advantage of EVPN by setting up ESI-Lag on distribution switches

#### Leaf / Access / Collapsed-Core
For leaf nodes in a EVPN topology, you’d have to configure the IPs for networks that would participate in EVPN. Optionally, VRFs to isolate traffic from one tenant verus another

> Body parameter

```json

  "overwrite": true,
  "pod_names": {

    "2": "default"
  },

      "mac": "5c5b35000003",
      "role": "collapsed-core"
    },
    {
      "mac": "5c5b35000004",

    }
  ]
}
```

`PUT /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/vc`

The VC creation and adding member switch API will update the device’s virtual chassis config which is applied after VC is formed to create JUNOS pre-provisioned virtual chassis configuration.

## Change to use preprovisioned VC
To switch the VC to use preprovisioned VC, enable preprovisioned in virtual_chassis config. Both vc_role master and backup will be matched to routing-engine role in Junos preprovisioned VC config. Member-id will be determined by the sequence of listed members.

Notice: to configure preprovisioned VC, every member of the VC must be presented in members or the confg push will be failed.

## Add new members
For models (e.g. EX4300 and up) having dedicated VC ports, it is easier to add new member switches into a VC by just connecting cables with the dedicated VC ports. Cloud will detect the new members and update the inventory.

For EX2300 VC, adding new members requires to follow the procedures below:
1. Powering on the new member switches and ensuring cables are not connected to any VC ports.
2. Claim or adopt all new member switches under the VC’s organization Inventory
3. Assign all new member switches to the same Site as the VC
4. Invoke vc command to add switches to the VC.
5. Connect the cables to the VC ports for these switches
6. After a while, the Org’s Inventory shows this new switches has been added into the VC.

## Removing member switch
To remove a member switch from the VC, following the procedures below:

1. Ensuring the VC is connected to the cloud first
2. Unplug the cable from the VC port of the switch
3. Waiting for the VC state (vc_state) of this switch is changed to not-present
4. Invoke update_vc with remove to remove this switch from the VC
5. The Org’s Inventory shows the switch is removed.

Please notice that member ID 0 (fpc0) cannot be removed. When a VC has two switches left, unpluging the cable may result in the situation that fpc0 becomes a line card (LC). When this situation is happened, please re-plug in the cable, wait for both switches becoming present (show virtual-chassis) and then removing the cable again.

## Renumber a member switch
When a member switch doesn’t work properly and needed to be replaced, the renumber API could be used. The following two types of renumber are supported:

1. Replace a non-fpc0 member switch
2. Replace fpc0. When fpc0 is relaced, PAPI device config and JUNOS config will be both updated.

For renumber to work, the following procedures are needed: 
1. Ensuring the VC is connected to the cloud and the state of the member switch to be replaced must be non present. 
2. Adding the new member switch to the VC 
3. Waiting for the VC state (vc_state) of this VC to be updated to API server 
4. Invoke vc with renumber to replace the new member switch from fpc X to

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "members": [
    {
      "mac": "aff827549235",
      "member": 0,
      "vc_ports": [
        "xe-0/1/1"
      ]
    },
    {
      "mac": "aff827549235",
      "member": 2,

        "xe-0/1/1"
      ]
    },

      ]
    },
    {
      "mac": "8396cd00888c",

      ]
    }
  ],

}
```

For models (e.g. EX3400 and up) having dedicated VC ports, it is easier to form a VC by just connecting cables with the dedicated VC ports. Cloud will detect the new VC and update the inventory.

In case that the user would like to choose the dedicated switch as a VC master. Or for EX2300-C-12P and EX2300-C-12T which doesn’t have dedicated VC ports, below are procedures to automate the VC creation:

1. Power on the switch that is choosen as the VC master first. And the powering on the other member switches.
2. Claim or adopt all these switches under the same organization’s Inventory
3. Assign these switches into the same Site
4. Invoke vc command on the switch choosen to be the VC master. For EX2300-C-12P, VC ports will be created automatically.
5. Connect the cables to the VC ports for these switches
6. Wait for the VC to be formed. The Org’s inventory will be updated for the new VC.

|» » vc_role|body|string|false|Optional. Only if `op`==`add`|
|» new-member|body|integer|false|Only if `op`==`renumber`|
|» op|body|string|false|none|

|---|---|
|» » vc_role|master|
|» » vc_role|backup|
|» » vc_role|linecard|
|» op|add|
|» op|remove|
|» op|renumber|

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/vc`

When all the member switches of VC are removed and only member ID 0 is left, the cloud would detect this situation and automatically changes the single switch to non-VC role.

For some unexpected cases that the VC is gone and disconncted, the API below could be used to change the state of VC’s switches to be standalone. After it is executed, all the switches will be shown as standalone switches under Inventory.

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/service_ping`

```json
{
    "subscribe": "/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/cmd"
}
```

```json
    "data": {
        "session": "session_id",
        "raw": "64 bytes from 23.211.0.110: seq=8 ttl=58 time=12.323 ms\n"
    }
}
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "count": 10,
  "host": "1.1.1.1",
  "service": "web-session"
}
```

## createSiteDeviceHaCluster

<a id="opIdcreateSiteDeviceHaCluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/ha \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "nodes": [
      {
        "mac": "aff827549235"
      },
      {
        "mac": "8396cd006c8c"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/ha`

Create HA Cluster
Both nodes has to be in the same site. We expect the user to configure ha_sync / ha_data port in port_configs already

### SRX cabling

see [Chassis Cluster User Guide for SRX Series Devices](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/chassis-cluster-security-devices/topics/concept/chassis-cluster-srx-series-node-interface-understanding.html) Here’s the recommended cabling.

#### SRX300

From ZTP / default state, ge-0/0/0 and ge-0/0/7 (SFP) are default WAN ports and will get DHCP IP. However, ge-0/0/0 becomes OOB/fxp0 after cluster is enabled (i.e. using it for reach Mist is not recommended)

1.  form cluster in UI
2.  configure ge-0/0/7,ge-1/0/7 for WAN (reth0)
3.  configure ge-0/0/2,ge-1/0/2 for ha_data
4.  configure ge-0/0/3- for LAN or additional WAN e.g.
    

``` json
{
    "port_config": {
        "ge-0/0/2,ge-1/0/2": {
            "usage": "ha_data"
        },
        "ge-0/0/7,ge-1/0/7": {
            "usage": "wan",
            "redundant": true,
            "reth_idx": 0,
            "ip_config": {"type": "dhcp"}
        },
    }
}

```

1.  connect ge-0/0/1 back to back for ha_control
2.  connect ge-0/0/2 back to back for ha_data
3.  connect both ge-0/0/7 to uplink switch to WAN and to reach Mist
4.  power up both devices
5.  it takes about 30 minutes for the cluster to form
    

#### SRX320

From ZTP / default state, ge-0/0/0, ge-0/0/7 (SFP) and cl-1/0/0 (LTE) are default WAN ports and will get DHCP IP. However, ge-0/0/0 becomes OOB/fxp0 after cluster is enabled (i.e. using it for reach Mist is not recommended)

##### ZTP via ge-0/0/7

Similar to SRX300

##### ZTP via cl-1/0/0 (LTE)

1.  form cluster in UI
2.  configure cl-1/0/0, cl-3/0/0 as WAN (reth0)
3.  configure ge-0/0/2,ge-3/0/2 for ha_data
4.  same as above
    

#### SRX340 / SRX345 / SRX380

SRX340/SRX345 has dedicated OOB/fxp0 ports

1.  form cluster in UI
2.  configure ge-0/0/0,ge-5/0/0 for WAN (reth0)
3.  configure ge-0/0/2,ge-5/0/2 for ha_data
4.  configure ge-0/0/3- for LAN or additional WAN
5.  connect ge-0/0/0 to uplink switch to WAN and to reach Mist
6.  connect ge-0/0/1 back-to-back for ha_control
7.  connect ge-0/0/2 back-to-back for ha_data (fabric); or for SRX380, xe-0/0/16 if 10G SFP+ is used
8.  connect ge-0/0/3- to LAN or additional WANs
    

#### SRX550

ge-0/0/0 becomes OOB/fxp0 after cluster is enabled, make suenable oob_ip_config as dhcp to maintain cloud connectivity

1.  connect ge-0/0/0 to reach Mist (after cluster is fully up, this port becomes OOB/fxp0)
2.  connect ge-0/0/1 back-to-back for ha_control
3.  connect ge-0/0/2 back-to-back for ha_data (fabric)
4.  connect ge-0/0/3 to WAN (after cluster is up, intended to be used for reth0)
5.  connect ge-0/0/4- to LAN or additional WANs
    

#### SRX1500

SRX1500 has, additionally, dedicated HA Control port

1.  form cluster in UI
2.  configure ge-0/0/0,ge-5/0/0 for WAN (reth0)
3.  configure ge-0/0/1,ge-5/0/1 for ha_data
4.  configure ge-0/0/2- for LAN or additional WAN
5.  connect dedicated ha_control back-to-back
6.  connect ge-0/0/0 to uplink switch to WAN and to reach Mist
7.  connect ge-0/0/1 back-to-back for ha_data
8.  connect ge-0/0/2- to LAN or additional WANs
    

#### SRX4100

SRX4100 has dedicated ha_control and ha_data (fabric) ports

1.  connect dedicated ha_control back-to-back
2.  connect dedicated ha_data back-to-back
3.  connect xe-0/0/0 to WAN to reach Mist
4.  connect xe-0/0/1- to LAN or additional WANs
    

#### VSRX

When standalone, VSRX has fxp0 as first Network Adapter, then ge-0/0/0-N When clustered, VSRX has fxp0, em0, then ge-0/0/0-N

1.  connect net0 (fxp0) to WAN to reach Mist
2.  connect net1 back-to-back for ha_control
3.  connect net2 (ge-0/0/0) back-to-back for ha_data (fab0/fab1)
4.  connect net3 (ge-0/0/1) to WAN, intended to be used for reth0
5.  connect net4 (ge-0/0/2) to LAN
    

SRX340/SRX345 has dedicated OOB/fxp0 ports VSRX has fxp0 as first Network Adapter, then ge-0/0/0-N

1.  connect ge-0/0/0 to WAN to reach Mist
2.  connect ge-0/0/1 back-to-back for ha_control
3.  connect ge-0/0/2 back-to-back for ha_data (fabric); or for SRX380, xe-0/0/16 if 10G SFP+ is used
4.  connect ge-0/0/3- to LAN or additional WANs
    

#### SRX550

ge-0/0/0 becomes OOB/fxp0 after cluster is enabled, make suenable oob_ip_config as dhcp to maintain cloud connectivity

1.  connect ge-0/0/0 to reach Mist (after cluster is fully up, this port becomes OOB/fxp0)
2.  connect ge-0/0/1 back-to-back for ha_control
3.  connect ge-0/0/2 back-to-back for ha_data (fabric)
4.  connect ge-0/0/3 to WAN (after cluster is up, intended to be used for reth0)
5.  connect ge-0/0/4- to LAN or additional WANs
    

#### SRX1500

SRX1500 has, additionally, dedicated HA Control port

1.  connect dedicated ha_control back-to-back
2.  connect ge-0/0/0 to WAN to reach mist
3.  connect ge-0/0/1 back-to-back for ha_data
4.  connect ge-0/0/2- to LAN or additional WANs
    

#### SRX4100

SRX4100 has dedicated ha_control and ha_data (fabric) ports

1.  connect dedicated ha_control back-to-back
2.  connect dedicated ha_data back-to-back
3.  connect xe-0/0/0 to WAN to reach Mist
4.  connect xe-0/0/1- to LAN or additional WANs

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "mac": "aff827549235"
    },
    {
      "mac": "8396cd006c8c"
    }
  ]
}
```

## arpFromDevice

<a id="opIdarpFromDevice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/arp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/arp`

ARP can be performed on the Device. The output will be available through websocket. As there can be multiple command issued against the same AP at the same time and the output all goes through the same websocket stream, session is introduced for demux.


#### Subscribe to Device Command outputs
`WS /api-ws/v1/stream`

```json
{
    "subscribe": "/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/cmd"
}
```
##### Example output from ws stream
```json
{ 
 "event": "data", 
 "channel": "/sites/4ac1dcf4-9d8b-7211-65c4-057819f0862b/devices/00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b350e0060/cmd", 
 "data": { 
   "session": "session_id", 
   "raw": 
   "Output": "\tMAC\t\tDEV\tVLAN\tRx Packets\t\t Rx Bytes\t\tTx Packets\t\t Tx Bytes\tFlows\tIdle sec\n-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------"
  } 
}
```

<h3 id="arpfromdevice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "session": "session_id"
}
```

<h3 id="arpfromdevice-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<h3 id="arpfromdevice-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|string|true|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

## pingFromDevice

<a id="opIdpingFromDevice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/ping \

  -d '{
    "count": 10,
    "host": "1.1.1.1"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/ping`

Ping from AP, Switch and SSR

Ping can be performed from the Device. The output will be available through websocket. As there can be multiple command issued against the same AP at the same time and the output all goes through the same websocket stream, session is introduced for demux.

#### Subscribe to Device Command outputs
`WS /api-ws/v1/stream`

```json
{
    "subscribe": "/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/cmd"
}
```
##### Example output from ws stream
```json
{
    "event": "data",
    "channel": "/sites/4ac1dcf4-9d8b-7211-65c4-057819f0862b/devices/00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b350e0060/cmd",
    "data": {
        "session": "session_id",
        "raw": "64 bytes from 23.211.0.110: seq=8 ttl=58 time=12.323 ms\n"
    }
}
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "count": 10,
  "host": "1.1.1.1"
}
```

<h3 id="pingfromdevice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|Request Body|
|» count|body|integer|false|none|
|» egress_interface|body|string|false|Interface through which packet needs to egress|
|» host|body|string(ipv4)|true|none|
|» size|body|integer|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "session": "session_id"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|end|integer|true|none|none|
|limit|integer|true|none|none|
|next|string|false|none|link to next set of results. If more results aren’t present, next is null.|
|results|[object]|true|none|none|
|» ap_mac|string|true|none|mac of the device that had strongest signal strength for ssid/bssid pair|
|» avg_rssi|number|true|none|average signal strength of ap_mac for ssid/bssid pair|
|» bssid|string|true|none|bssid of the network detected as threat|
|» channel|string|true|none|channel over which ap_mac heard ssid/bssid pair|
|» delta_x|number|false|none|X position relative to the reporting AP (`ap_mac`)|
|» delta_y|number|false|none|Y position relative to the reporting AP (`ap_mac`)|
|» num_aps|integer|true|none|num of aps that heard the ssid/bssid pair|
|» seen_on_lan|boolean|false|none|whether the reporting AP see a wireless client (on LAN) connecting to it|
|» ssid|string|false|none|ssid of the network detected as threat|
|» times_heard|integer|false|none|represents number of times the pair was heard in the interval. Each count roughly corresponds to a minute.|
|start|integer|true|none|none|

## getSiteMachineLearningCurrentStat

<a id="opIdgetSiteMachineLearningCurrentStat"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/location/ml/current \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/location/ml/current`

Get Machine Learning Current Stat
For each VBLE AP, it has ML model parameters (e.g. Path-loss-estimate, Intercept) as well as completion indicators (Level and PercentageComplete). For the completeness, ML takes N sample to finish its first level and use N*0.25 samples to complete each successive level. When a device is moved, the completeness will be reset as it has to re-learn.

<h3 id="getsitemachinelearningcurrentstat-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|map_id|query|string|false|map_id (as filter, optional)|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "current": {
      "Android": {
        "completed": 36,
        "int": -6,
        "level": 3,
        "ple": -3,
        "quality": "4",
        "src": "device",
        "timestamp": 1442854794
      },
      "iOS": {
        "completed": 16,
        "int": -6,
        "level": 6,
        "ple": -3,
        "quality": "2",
        "src": "default",
        "timestamp": 1442854704
      },
      "iPod": {
        "int": -10,
        "overwrite": true,
        "ple": -5,
        "src": "overwrite"
      }
    },
    "device_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1"
  },
  {
    "beacon_id": "7913f032-aab4-c3ae-e83e-5a2756ef4d40",
    "current": {
      "iOS": {
        "completed": 16,
        "int": -6,
        "level": 6,
        "ple": -3,
        "quality": "last",
        "src": "device",
        "timestamp": 1442854704
      }
    }
  }
]
```

<h3 id="getsitemachinelearningcurrentstat-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<h3 id="getsitemachinelearningcurrentstat-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|

apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

## importSiteMaps

<a id="opIdimportSiteMaps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/maps/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'auto_deviceprofile_assignment=true' \
  -F 'csv=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'json={"import_all_floorpans":false,"import_height":true,"import_orientation":true,"site_id":"72771e6a-6f5e-4de4-a5b9-1266c4197811","vendor_name":"ekahau"}'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/maps/import`

Import data from files is a multipart POST which has an file, an optional json, and an optional csv, to create floorplan, assign matching inventory to specific site, place ap if name or mac matches

# CSV File Format
```csv
Vendor AP name,Mist AP Mac
US Office AP-2 - 5c:5b:35:00:00:02,5c5b35000002
``` 

> Body parameter

```yaml
auto_deviceprofile_assignment: true
csv: string
file: string
json:
  import_all_floorpans: false
  import_height: true
  import_orientation: true
  site_id: "72771e6a-6f5e-4de4-a5b9-1266c4197811"
  vendor_name: ekahau
```

<h3 id="importsitemaps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» auto_deviceprofile_assignment|body|boolean|false|boolean, whether to auto assign device to deviceprofile by name|
|» csv|body|string(binary)|false|csv file for ap name mapping, optional|
|» file|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» json|body|object|false|none|
|» » import_all_floorpans|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » import_height|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » import_orientation|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » site_id|body|string(uuid)|true|none|
|» » vendor_name|body|string|true|none|

## runSiteApAutoplacement

<a id="opIdrunSiteApAutoplacement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/maps/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/auto_placement \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "device_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "force_collection": false
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/maps/{map_id}/auto_placement`

This API is called to trigger a map for auto placement. For auto placement feature to work, RTT-FTM data need to be collected from the APs on the map. This scan is disruptive and therefore the user must be notified of service disrution during the functioning of auto placement Repeated POST to this endpoint while a map is still running will be rejected.

List of devices to provide suggestions for is an optional parameter that can be given to this API. This will provide autoplacement suggestions only for the devices specified. If no list of devices is provided, all APs asociated with that map are considered by default

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "device_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "force_collection": false
}
```

<h3 id="runsiteapautoplacement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|map_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» device_ids|body|[string]|false|list of device macs|
|» force_collection|body|boolean|false|* If `force_collection`==`false`: the API Iattempts to start localization with existing data. <br>* If `force_collection`==`true`: maintenance the API attempts to start orchestration.|

<h3 id="runsiteapautoplacement-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Autoplacement Process has begun for this map|None|
|400|Bad Request|* Map has less than 3 APs associated with it to perform auto placement <br>* Insufficient anchors for auto placement. 3 required<br>* Auto AP Placement is already in progress for this Map<br>* Autoplacement data does not exist or has gone stale|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
apiToken, basicAuth
</aside>

## replaceSiteMapImage

<a id="opIdreplaceSiteMapImage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/maps/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/replace \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'json={"transform":{"rotate":0,"scale":0,"x":0,"y":0}}'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/maps/{map_id}/replace`

Replace Map Image


This works like an PUT where the image will be replaced. If transform is provided, all the locations of the objects on the map (AP, Zone, Vbeacon, Beacon) will be transformed as well (relative to the new Map)

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
json:
  transform:
    rotate: 0
    scale: 0
    x: 0
    y: 0
```

<h3 id="replacesitemapimage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|map_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|none|
|» json|body|object|false|none|
|» » transform|body|object|false|If `transform` is provided, all the locations of the objects on the map (AP, Zone, Vbeacon, Beacon) will be transformed as well (relative to the new Map)|
|» » » rotate|body|number|false|none|
|» » » scale|body|number|false|none|
|» » » x|body|number|false|none|
|» » » y|body|number|false|none|

> Example responses

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="replacesitemapimage-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

```bash
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/maps/{map_id}/set_map`

This API can be used to assign a list of AP Macs associated with site_id to the specified map_id. Note that map_id must be associated with corresponding site_id. This API obeys the following rules 
1. if AP is unassigned to any Map, it gets associated with map_id 
2. Any moved APs are returned in the response 
3. If the AP is considered a locked AP, no action will be taken

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "device_ids": [
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b35000001",
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b35584a6f"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="bulkassignsiteapstomap-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|map_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» device_ids|body|[string]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "locked": [
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b35000001"
  ],
  "moved": [
    "00000000-0000-0000-1000-5c5b35584a6f"
  ]
}
```

## startSitePacketCapture

<a id="opIdstartSitePacketCapture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/pcaps/capture \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "client_mac": "60a10a773412",
    "duration": 600,
    "includes_mcast": false,
    "max_pkt_len": 128,
    "num_packets": 100,
    "type": "new_assoc"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/pcaps/capture`

Initiate a Packet Capture

The output will be available through websocket. As there can be multiple command issued against the same AP at the same time and the output all goes through the same websocket stream, session is introduced for demux.

#### Subscribe to Device Command outputs
`WS /api-ws/v1/stream`

```json
{
    subscribe: "/sites/{site_id}/pcaps"
}
```

## countSiteByDistringAttributesOfSkyatpEvents

<a id="opIdcountSiteByDistringAttributesOfSkyatpEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/skyatp/events/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/skyatp/events/count`

Count by Distinct Attributes of Skyatp Events (WIP)

<h3 id="countsitebydistringattributesofskyatpevents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|distinct|query|string|false|none|
|type|query|string|false|event type, e.g. cc, fs, mw|
|mac|query|string|false|client MAC|
|device_mac|query|string|false|device MAC|
|threat_level|query|integer|false|threat level|
|ip address|query|string(ipv4)|false|none|
|page|query|integer|false|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|none|
|start|query|integer|false|none|
|end|query|integer|false|none|
|duration|query|string|false|For historical stats and/or logs where time range is needed, you can specify the time range in a few different ways:<br>  * ?start=1430000000&end=1430864000	specify the start / end<br>  * ?end=1430864000&duration=1d	specify end time and duration<br>  * ?duration=1d	specify duration, end will be now() in seconds|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|distinct|type|
|distinct|mac|
|distinct|device_mac|
|distinct|threat_level|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "distinct": "string",
  "end": 0,
  "limit": 0,
  "percentage": 0,
  "results": [
    {
      "count": 0,
      "property": "string"
    }
  ],
  "start": 0,
  "total": 0
}
```

<h3 id="countsitebydistringattributesofskyatpevents-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

## triggerSiteSwitchRadiusSyntheticTest

<a id="opIdstartSiteSwitchRadiusSyntheticTest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/devices/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/check_radius_server \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "password": "string",
    "profile": "dot1x",
    "user": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices/{device_id}/check_radius_server`

Ping test from the AP to confirm ‘reachability’ of the Radius server. Utilize Juniper EX switch(to which an AP is connected to) radius test capabilities to get details on the Radius Server ‘availability’.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "password": "string",
  "profile": "dot1x",
  "user": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="triggersiteswitchradiussynthetictest-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|device_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» password|body|string|true|Specify the password associated with the username|
|» profile|body|string|false|Specify the access profile associated with the subscriber|
|» user|body|string|true|Specify the subscriber username to test|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "session": "session_id"
}
```

<h3 id="triggersiteswitchradiussynthetictest-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|string|true|none|none|

## createSiteWebhook

<a id="opIdcreateSiteWebhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/sites/000000ab-00ab-00ab-00ab-0000000000ab/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "headers": {},
    "name": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "splunk_token": "string",
    "topics": [
      "location"
    ],
    "type": "http-post",
    "url": "string",
    "verify_cert": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/webhooks`

Webhook defines a webhook, modeled after [github’s model](https://developer.github.com/webhooks/).

There is two types of webhooks:
* webhooks ([examples](https://www.postman.com/juniper-mist/workspace/mist-systems-s-public-workspace/folder/224925-be01e694-7253-4195-8563-78e2a745e114))
* raw data webhooks ([examples](https://www.postman.com/juniper-mist/workspace/mist-systems-s-public-workspace/folder/224925-e2d5d5f8-4bdb-4efc-93e4-90f4b33d0b2b))

##### Webhooks
Webhooks can be configured at the org level (subset of topics only) and at the site level. It is possible to have multiple topics in the same webhook configuration and/or to have multiple webhooks configured at the same time.

##### Client Raw Data Webhooks
Raw data webhooks are a special subset of webhooks that provide insight into raw data packets emitted by a client, identified by their advertising MAC address (assets, discovered ble, connected wifi, unconnected wifi). The data that client raw data webhooks encompasses are reporting AP information, RSSI Data, and any special packets/telemetry packets that the client may emit. Note that client raw webhooks are the raw data coming from the client and do not contain the X,Y location data of the client. In order to get the location data for a client please see our location webhooks. Clients can be identified uniquely across these client raw data topics and location webhook topic using MAC address as the Unique identifier (client identifier).

###### Client Raw Data Webhooks Topics
Topics that correspond to client raw data for different client types. 
* `asset-raw-rssi` - Raw data from packets emitted by named and filtered assets 
* `discovered-raw-rssi` - Raw data from packets emitted by passive BLE devices 
* `wifi-conn-raw` - Raw data from packets emitted by connected devices 
* `wifi-unconn-raw` - Raw data from packets emitted by unconnected devices (passive)

###### Rules for configuring client raw data webhooks
1. Only one instance of a webhook object containing a client raw data webhook topic is allowed. (a site level entry will override an org level entry for the client raw data webhook topic in question)
2. Only one client raw data webhook topic is allowed per `http-post` message to webhooks api


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "headers": {},
  "name": "string",
  "secret": "string",
  "splunk_token": "string",
  "topics": [
    "location"
  ],
  "type": "http-post",
  "url": "string",
  "verify_cert": true
}
```

<h3 id="createsitewebhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[webhook](#schemawebhook)|false|Request Body|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|whether webhook is enabled|
|» headers|body|object \| null|false|custom headers : the headers name and value must be string, total bytes of headers name and value must be less than 1000|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|name of the webhook|
|» secret|body|string \| null|false|only if `type`=`http-post`<br>when `secret` is provided, two HTTP headers will be added:<br>  * X-Mist-Signature-v2: HMAC_SHA256(secret, body)<br>  * X-Mist-Signature: HMAC_SHA1(secret, body)|
|» splunk_token|body|string \| null|false|splunk token (If splunk_token is not defined for a type Splunk webhook, it will not send, regardless if the webhook receiver is configured to accept it.)|
|» topics|body|[string]|false|N.B. For org webhooks, only device-events/alarms/audits/client-join/client-sessions/nac-sessions topics are supported.|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|http-post (default) / splunk / google-pubsub / aws-sns|
|» url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» verify_cert|body|boolean|false|when url uses HTTPS, whether to verify the certificate|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» topics|alarms|
|» topics|asset-raw|
|» topics|asset-raw-rssi|
|» topics|audits|
|» topics|client-join|
|» topics|client-sessions|
|» topics|device-events|
|» topics|device-updowns|
|» topics|discovered-raw-rssi|
|» topics|location|
|» topics|mxedge-events|
|» topics|nac-sessions|
|» topics|occupancy-alerts|
|» topics|rssizone|
|» topics|sdkclient-scan-data|
|» topics|vbeacon|
|» topics|wifi-conn-raw|
|» topics|wifi-unconn-raw|
|» topics|zone|
|» type|http-post|
|» type|splunk|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created_time": 0,
  "enabled": true,
  "headers": {},
  "id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "modified_time": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "org_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "secret": "string",
  "site_id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
  "splunk_token": "string",
  "topics": [
    "location"
  ],
  "type": "http-post",
  "url": "string",
  "verify_cert": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "Webhook already configured for special location topic",
  "webhook_id": "f1ff49e8-9f77-420a-9854-c7de46d7cf80"
}
```

<h3 id="createsitewebhook-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[webhook](#schemawebhook)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|Inline|

Status Code **400**

|webhook_id|string|false|none|none|

|» topics|body|[string]|false|N.B. For org webhooks, only device-events/alarms/audits/client-join/client-sessions/nac-sessions topics are supported.|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|http-post (default) / splunk / google-pubsub / aws-sns|
|» url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» verify_cert|body|boolean|false|when url uses HTTPS, whether to verify the certificate|

|» topics|vbeacon|
|» topics|wifi-conn-raw|
|» topics|wifi-unconn-raw|
|» topics|zone|
|» type|http-post|
|» type|splunk|

<h3 id="createsitewlan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[wlan](#schemawlan)|false|Request Body|
|» acct_interim_interval|body|integer|false|how frequently should interim accounting be reported, 60-65535. default is 0 (use one specified in Access-Accept request from RADIUS Server). Very frequent messages can affect the performance of the radius server, 600 and up is recommended when enabled|
|» acct_servers|body|[[acct_server](#schemaacct_server)]|false|list of RADIUS accounting servers, optional, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|» airwatch|body|[wlan_airwatch](#schemawlan_airwatch)|false|airwatch wlan settings|
|» allow_ipv6_ndp|body|boolean|false|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows or disallows ipv6 Neighbor Discovery packets to go through|
|» allow_mdns|body|boolean|false|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows mDNS / Bonjour packets to go through|
|» allow_ssdp|body|boolean|false|only applicable when `limit_bcast`==`tru`e, which allows SSDP|
|» ap_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|list of device ids|
|» app_limit|body|object|false|bandwidth limiting for apps (applies to up/down)|
|» » apps|body|object|false|map from app key to bandwidth in kbps. app key defined in Get Application List|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » wxtag_ids|body|object|false|map from wxtag_id of Hostname Wxlan Tags to bandwidth in kbps|
|» app_qos|body|[wlan_app_qos](#schemawlan_app_qos)|false|app qos wlan settings|
|» apply_to|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» arp_filter|body|boolean|false|whether to enable smart arp filter|
|» auth|body|[wlan_auth](#schemawlan_auth)|false|authentication wlan settings|
|» auth_server_selection|body|string \| null|false|When ordered, AP will prefer and go back to the first server if possible|
|» auth_servers|body|[[auth_server](#schemaauth_server)]|false|list of RADIUS authentication servers, at least one is needed if `auth type`==`eap`, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|» auth_servers_nas_id|body|string \| null|false|optional, up to 48 bytes, will be dynamically generated if not provided. used only for authentication servers|
|» auth_servers_nas_ip|body|string \| null|false|optional, NAS-IP-ADDRESS to use|
|» auth_servers_retries|body|integer|false|radius auth session retries|
|» auth_servers_timeout|body|integer|false|radius auth session timeout|
|» band|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** `band` is deprecated and kept for backward compability. Use bands instead|
|» band_steer|body|boolean|false|whether to enable band_steering, this works only when band==both|
|» band_steer_force_band5|body|boolean|false|force dual-band capable client to connect to 5G|
|» bands|body|[string]|false|list of radios that the wlan should apply to|
|» block_blacklist_clients|body|boolean|false|whether to block the clients in the blacklist (up to first 256 macs)|
|» bonjour|body|[wlan_bonjour](#schemawlan_bonjour)|false|bonjour gateway wlan settings|
|» cisco_cwa|body|[wlan_cisco_cwa](#schemawlan_cisco_cwa)|false|Cisco CWA (central web authentication) required RADIUS with COA in order to work. See CWA: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/security/identity-services-engine/115732-central-web-auth-00.html<br>|
|» client_limit_down|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» client_limit_down_enabled|body|boolean|false|if downlink limiting per-client is enabled|
|» client_limit_up|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» client_limit_up_enabled|body|boolean|false|if uplink limiting per-client is enabled|
|» coa_servers|body|[[coa_server](#schemacoa_server)]|false|list of COA (change of authorization) servers, optional|
|» disable_11ax|body|boolean|false|some old WLAN drivers may not be compatible|
|» disable_ht_vht_rates|body|boolean|false|to disable ht or vht rates|
|» disable_uapsd|body|boolean|false|whether to disable U-APSD|
|» disable_v1_roam_notify|body|boolean|false|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|» disable_v2_roam_notify|body|boolean|false|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|» disable_wmm|body|boolean|false|whether to disable WMM|
|» dns_server_rewrite|body|object \| null|false|for radius_group-based DNS server (rewrite DNS request depending on the Group RADIUS server returns)|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » radius_groups|body|object|false|map between radius_group and the desired DNS server (IPv4 only)|
|» dtim|body|integer|false|none|
|» dynamic_psk|body|object \| null|false|for dynamic PSK where we get per-user PSK from Radius<br>dynamic_psk allows PSK to be selected at runtime depending on context (wlan/site/user/...) thus following configurations are assumed (currently)<br>- PSK will come from RADIUS server<br>- AP sends client MAC as username ans password (i.e. `enable_mac_auth` is assumed)<br>- AP sends BSSID:SSID as Caller-Station-ID<br>- `auth_servers` is required<br>- PSK will come from cloud WLC if source is cloud_psks<br>- default_psk will be used if cloud WLC is not available<br>- `multi_psk_only` and `psk` is ignored<br>- `pairwise` can only be wpa2-ccmp (for now, wpa3 support on the roadmap)|
|» » default_psk|body|string|false|default PSK to use if cloud WLC is not available, 8-63 characters|
|» » default_vlan_id|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » source|body|string|false|none|
|» » vlan_ids|body|[integer \| null]|false|none|
|» dynamic_vlan|body|object \| null|false|for 802.1x|
|» » default_vlan_id|body|integer \| null|false|vlan_id to use when there’s no match from RADIUS|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether to enable dynamic vlan|
|» » local_vlan_ids|body|[integer \| null]|false|vlan_ids to be locally bridged|
|» » type|body|string \| null|false|standard (using Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, widely supported), airespace-interface-name (Airespace/Cisco)|
|» » vlans|body|object|false|map between vlan_id (as string) to airespace interface names (comma-separated) or null for stndard mapping|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» enable_local_keycaching|body|boolean|false|enable AP-AP keycaching via multicast|
|» enable_wireless_bridging|body|boolean|false|whether to enable wireless bridging, which allows more broadcast packets to go through<br>(allows forwarding of DHCP response to client not associated with the AP)|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|if this wlan is enabled|
|» hide_ssid|body|boolean|false|whether to hide SSID in beacon|
|» hostname_ie|body|boolean|false|include hostname inside IE in AP beacons / probe responses|
|» hotspot20|body|[wlan_hotspot_20](#schemawlan_hotspot_20)|false|hostspot 2.0 wlan settings|
|» interface|body|string|false|where this WLAN will be connected to|
|» isolation|body|boolean|false|whether to allow clients to talk to each other|
|» l2_isolation|body|boolean|false|if isolation is enabled, whether to deny clients to talk to L2 on the LAN|
|» legacy_overds|body|boolean|false|legacy devices requires the Over-DS (for Fast BSS Transition) bit set (while our chip doesn’t support it). Warning! Enabling this will cause problem for iOS devices.|
|» limit_bcast|body|boolean|false|whether to limit broadcast packets going to wireless (i.e. only allow certain bcast packets to go through)|
|» limit_probe_response|body|boolean|false|limit probe response base on some heuristic rules|
|» max_idletime|body|integer|false|max idle time in seconds|
|» mist_nac|body|object|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|when enabled:<br>* `auth_servers` is ignored<br>* `acct_servers` is ignored<br>* `auth_servers_*` are ignored<br>* `coa_servers` is ignored<br>* `radsec` is ignored|
|» mxtunnel|body|object|false|when `interface`=`site_medge`, the definition of the Mist Tunnels (key is the name)|
|» mxtunnel_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|when `interface`=`mxtunnel`, id of the Mist Tunnel|
|» mxtunnel_name|body|string \| null|false|when `interface`=`site_medge`, name of the mxtunnel that in mxtunnels under Site Setting|
|» no_static_dns|body|boolean|false|whether to only allow client to use DNS that we’ve learned from DHCP response|
|» no_static_ip|body|boolean|false|whether to only allow client that we’ve learned from DHCP exchange to talk|
|» portal|body|[wlan_portal](#schemawlan_portal)|false|portal wlan settings|
|» portal_allowed_hostnames|body|[string]|false|list of hostnames without http(s):// (matched by substring)|
|» portal_allowed_subnets|body|[string]|false|list of CIDRs|
|» portal_api_secret|body|string \| null|false|api secret (auto-generated) that can be used to sign guest authorization requests|
|» portal_denied_hostnames|body|[string]|false|list of hostnames without http(s):// (matched by substring), this takes precedence over portal_allowed_hostnames|
|» portal_image|body|string(uri) \| null|false|Url of portal background image|
|» portal_sso_url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» portal_template_url|body|string \| null|false|N.B portal_template will be forked out of wlan objects soon. To fetch portal_template, please query portal_template_url. To update portal_template, use Wlan Portal Template.|
|» qos|body|object|false|none|
|» » class|body|string|false|none|
|» » overwrite|body|boolean|false|whether to overwrite QoS|
|» radsec|body|[radsec](#schemaradsec)|false|Radsec settings|
|» rateset|body|object|false|none|
|» » 5|body|[wlan_datarates](#schemawlan_datarates)|false|data rates wlan settings|
|» » 24|body|[wlan_datarates](#schemawlan_datarates)|false|data rates wlan settings|
|» roam_mode|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» schedule|body|object|false|WLAN operating schedule, default is disabled|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hours|body|object|false|time ranges, the key is mon / tue / wed / thu / fri / sat / sun, the value is time range in “HH:MM-HH:MM” (24-hour format), the minimum resolution is 30 minute|
|» sle_excluded|body|boolean|false|whether to exclude this WLAN from SLE metrics|
|» ssid|body|string|true|the name of the SSID|
|» template_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|
|» thumbnail|body|string(uri) \| null|false|Url of portal background image thumbnail|
|» use_eapol_v1|body|boolean|false|if `auth.type`==’eap’ or ‘psk’, should only be set for legacy client, such as pre-2004, 802.11b devices|
|» vlan_enabled|body|boolean|false|if vlan tagging is enabled|
|» vlan_id|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» vlan_ids|body|[integer \| null]|false|list of VLAN ids|
|» vlan_pooling|body|boolean|false|vlan pooling allows AP to place client on different VLAN using a deterministic algorithm|
|» wlan_limit_down|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» wlan_limit_down_enabled|body|boolean|false|if downlink limiting for whole wlan is enabled|
|» wlan_limit_up|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» wlan_limit_up_enabled|body|boolean|false|if uplink limiting for whole wlan is enabled|
|» wxtag_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|list of wxtag_ids|

|» wxtunnel_remote_id|body|string \| null|false|when `interface`=`wxtunnel`, remote tunnel identifier|

<h3 id="updatesitewlan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|wlan_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[wlan](#schemawlan)|false|Request Body|
|» acct_interim_interval|body|integer|false|how frequently should interim accounting be reported, 60-65535. default is 0 (use one specified in Access-Accept request from RADIUS Server). Very frequent messages can affect the performance of the radius server, 600 and up is recommended when enabled|
|» acct_servers|body|[[acct_server](#schemaacct_server)]|false|list of RADIUS accounting servers, optional, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|» airwatch|body|[wlan_airwatch](#schemawlan_airwatch)|false|airwatch wlan settings|
|» allow_ipv6_ndp|body|boolean|false|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows or disallows ipv6 Neighbor Discovery packets to go through|
|» allow_mdns|body|boolean|false|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows mDNS / Bonjour packets to go through|
|» allow_ssdp|body|boolean|false|only applicable when `limit_bcast`==`tru`e, which allows SSDP|
|» ap_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|list of device ids|
|» app_limit|body|object|false|bandwidth limiting for apps (applies to up/down)|
|» » apps|body|object|false|map from app key to bandwidth in kbps. app key defined in Get Application List|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » wxtag_ids|body|object|false|map from wxtag_id of Hostname Wxlan Tags to bandwidth in kbps|
|» app_qos|body|[wlan_app_qos](#schemawlan_app_qos)|false|app qos wlan settings|
|» apply_to|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» arp_filter|body|boolean|false|whether to enable smart arp filter|
|» auth|body|[wlan_auth](#schemawlan_auth)|false|authentication wlan settings|
|» auth_server_selection|body|string \| null|false|When ordered, AP will prefer and go back to the first server if possible|
|» auth_servers|body|[[auth_server](#schemaauth_server)]|false|list of RADIUS authentication servers, at least one is needed if `auth type`==`eap`, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|» auth_servers_nas_id|body|string \| null|false|optional, up to 48 bytes, will be dynamically generated if not provided. used only for authentication servers|
|» auth_servers_nas_ip|body|string \| null|false|optional, NAS-IP-ADDRESS to use|
|» auth_servers_retries|body|integer|false|radius auth session retries|
|» auth_servers_timeout|body|integer|false|radius auth session timeout|
|» band|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** `band` is deprecated and kept for backward compability. Use bands instead|
|» band_steer|body|boolean|false|whether to enable band_steering, this works only when band==both|
|» band_steer_force_band5|body|boolean|false|force dual-band capable client to connect to 5G|
|» bands|body|[string]|false|list of radios that the wlan should apply to|
|» block_blacklist_clients|body|boolean|false|whether to block the clients in the blacklist (up to first 256 macs)|
|» bonjour|body|[wlan_bonjour](#schemawlan_bonjour)|false|bonjour gateway wlan settings|
|» cisco_cwa|body|[wlan_cisco_cwa](#schemawlan_cisco_cwa)|false|Cisco CWA (central web authentication) required RADIUS with COA in order to work. See CWA: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/security/identity-services-engine/115732-central-web-auth-00.html<br>|
|» client_limit_down|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» client_limit_down_enabled|body|boolean|false|if downlink limiting per-client is enabled|
|» client_limit_up|body|integer|false|kbps|
|» client_limit_up_enabled|body|boolean|false|if uplink limiting per-client is enabled|
|» coa_servers|body|[[coa_server](#schemacoa_server)]|false|list of COA (change of authorization) servers, optional|
|» disable_11ax|body|boolean|false|some old WLAN drivers may not be compatible|
|» disable_ht_vht_rates|body|boolean|false|to disable ht or vht rates|
|» disable_uapsd|body|boolean|false|whether to disable U-APSD|
|» disable_v1_roam_notify|body|boolean|false|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|» disable_v2_roam_notify|body|boolean|false|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|» disable_wmm|body|boolean|false|whether to disable WMM|
|» dns_server_rewrite|body|object \| null|false|for radius_group-based DNS server (rewrite DNS request depending on the Group RADIUS server returns)|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » radius_groups|body|object|false|map between radius_group and the desired DNS server (IPv4 only)|
|» dtim|body|integer|false|none|
|» dynamic_psk|body|object \| null|false|for dynamic PSK where we get per-user PSK from Radius<br>dynamic_psk allows PSK to be selected at runtime depending on context (wlan/site/user/...) thus following configurations are assumed (currently)<br>- PSK will come from RADIUS server<br>- AP sends client MAC as username ans password (i.e. `enable_mac_auth` is assumed)<br>- AP sends BSSID:SSID as Caller-Station-ID<br>- `auth_servers` is required<br>- PSK will come from cloud WLC if source is cloud_psks<br>- default_psk will be used if cloud WLC is not available<br>- `multi_psk_only` and `psk` is ignored<br>- `pairwise` can only be wpa2-ccmp (for now, wpa3 support on the roadmap)|
|» » default_psk|body|string|false|default PSK to use if cloud WLC is not available, 8-63 characters|
|» » default_vlan_id|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » source|body|string|false|none|
|» » vlan_ids|body|[integer \| null]|false|none|
|» dynamic_vlan|body|object \| null|false|for 802.1x|
|» » default_vlan_id|body|integer \| null|false|vlan_id to use when there’s no match from RADIUS|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether to enable dynamic vlan|
|» » local_vlan_ids|body|[integer \| null]|false|vlan_ids to be locally bridged|
|» » type|body|string \| null|false|standard (using Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, widely supported), airespace-interface-name (Airespace/Cisco)|
|» » vlans|body|object|false|map between vlan_id (as string) to airespace interface names (comma-separated) or null for stndard mapping|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» enable_local_keycaching|body|boolean|false|enable AP-AP keycaching via multicast|
|» enable_wireless_bridging|body|boolean|false|whether to enable wireless bridging, which allows more broadcast packets to go through<br>(allows forwarding of DHCP response to client not associated with the AP)|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|if this wlan is enabled|
|» hide_ssid|body|boolean|false|whether to hide SSID in beacon|
|» hostname_ie|body|boolean|false|include hostname inside IE in AP beacons / probe responses|
|» hotspot20|body|[wlan_hotspot_20](#schemawlan_hotspot_20)|false|hostspot 2.0 wlan settings|
|» interface|body|string|false|where this WLAN will be connected to|
|» isolation|body|boolean|false|whether to allow clients to talk to each other|
|» l2_isolation|body|boolean|false|if isolation is enabled, whether to deny clients to talk to L2 on the LAN|
|» legacy_overds|body|boolean|false|legacy devices requires the Over-DS (for Fast BSS Transition) bit set (while our chip doesn’t support it). Warning! Enabling this will cause problem for iOS devices.|
|» limit_bcast|body|boolean|false|whether to limit broadcast packets going to wireless (i.e. only allow certain bcast packets to go through)|
|» limit_probe_response|body|boolean|false|limit probe response base on some heuristic rules|
|» max_idletime|body|integer|false|max idle time in seconds|
|» mist_nac|body|object|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|when enabled:<br>* `auth_servers` is ignored<br>* `acct_servers` is ignored<br>* `auth_servers_*` are ignored<br>* `coa_servers` is ignored<br>* `radsec` is ignored|
|» mxtunnel|body|object|false|when `interface`=`site_medge`, the definition of the Mist Tunnels (key is the name)|
|» mxtunnel_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|when `interface`=`mxtunnel`, id of the Mist Tunnel|
|» mxtunnel_name|body|string \| null|false|when `interface`=`site_medge`, name of the mxtunnel that in mxtunnels under Site Setting|
|» no_static_dns|body|boolean|false|whether to only allow client to use DNS that we’ve learned from DHCP response|
|» no_static_ip|body|boolean|false|whether to only allow client that we’ve learned from DHCP exchange to talk|
|» portal|body|[wlan_portal](#schemawlan_portal)|false|portal wlan settings|
|» portal_allowed_hostnames|body|[string]|false|list of hostnames without http(s):// (matched by substring)|

|» portal_image|body|string(uri) \| null|false|Url of portal background image|
|» portal_sso_url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» portal_template_url|body|string \| null|false|N.B portal_template will be forked out of wlan objects soon. To fetch portal_template, please query portal_template_url. To update portal_template, use Wlan Portal Template.|
|» qos|body|object|false|none|
|» » class|body|string|false|none|

|» radsec|body|[radsec](#schemaradsec)|false|Radsec settings|

|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|none|

## deleteSiteWlan

<a id="opIddeleteSiteWlan"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/api/v1/utils/test_telstra \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

`GET /api/v1/utils/test_telstra`

Allows validation of Telstra sms gateway credentials.

In case of success, a text message confirming successful setup should be received. In case of error, telstra error message are returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "telstra_client_id": "123456",
  "telstra_client_secret": "abcdef",
  "to": "+911122334455"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» telstra_client_id|body|string|true|Telstra client id|
|» telstra_client_secret|body|string|true|Telstra client secret|
|» to|body|string|true|Phone number of the recipient of SMS with country code|

```json
{}
```

Create Site WxLan Tunnel

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dmvpn": {
    "enabled": true,
    "holding_time": 0,
    "host_routes": [
      "string"
    ]
  },
  "for_mgmt": true,
  "hello_interval": 1,
  "hello_retries": 3,
  "hostname": "string",
  "ipsec": {

  },
  "is_static": true,
  "mtu": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "peers": [

  ],

  "secret": "string",
  "sessions": [
    {
      "ap_as_session_id": "string",
      "comment": "string",
      "enable_cookie": true,
      "ethertype": "ethernet",
      "local_session_id": 1,
      "pseudo_802.1ad_enabled": true,
      "remote_id": "string",
      "remote_session_id": 1,
      "use_ap_as_session_ids": true
    }
  ],
  "udp_port": 0,
  "use_udp": true
}
```

<h3 id="createsitewxtunnel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|site_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[wxlan_tunnel](#schemawxlan_tunnel)|false|Request Body|
|» dmvpn|body|object|false|Dynamic Multipoint VPN configurations|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether DMVPN is enabled|
|» » holding_time|body|integer|false|optional; the holding time for NHRP ‘registration requests’ and ‘resolution replies’ sent from the Mist AP (in seconds); default 600|
|» » host_routes|body|[string]|false|optional; list of IPv4 DMVPN peer host ip-addresses to which traffic is forwarded|
|» for_mgmt|body|boolean|false|determined during creation time and cannot be toggled. A management tunnel cannot be used by wxlan rule or by wlan|
|» hello_interval|body|integer|false|in seconds, used as heartbeat to detect if a tunnel is alive. AP will try another peer after missing N hellos specified by hello_retries.|
|» hello_retries|body|integer|false|none|
|» hostname|body|string|false|optional, overwrite the hostname in SCCRQ control message, default is “” or null, %H and %M can be used, which will be replace with corresponding values:<br>* %H: name of the ap if provided (and will be stripped so it can be used for hostname) and fallbacks to MAC<br>* %M: MAC (e.g. 5c5b350e0060)|
|» ipsec|body|object|false|IPSec-related configurations; requires DMVPN be enabled|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether ipsec is enabled, requires DMVPN be enabled|
|» » psk|body|string|true|ipsec pre-shared key|
|» is_static|body|boolean|false|whether it’s static/unmanaged (i.e. no control session). As the session configurations are not compatible, cannot be toggled.|
|» mtu|body|integer|false|0 to enable PMTU, 552-1500 to start PMTU with a lower MTU|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the tunnel|
|» org_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» peers|body|[string]|false|list of remote peers’ IP or hostname|
|» router_id|body|string|false|optional, overwrite the router-id in SCCRQ control message, default is “0” or null, can also be an IPv4 address|
|» secret|body|string|false|secret, ‘’ if no auth is used|
|» sessions|body|[object]|false|sessions to be established with the tunnel. Has to be >= 1 in order for this tunnel to be useful. For management tunnel, it can only have 1|
|» » ap_as_session_id|body|string|false|if `use_ap_as_session_ids`==`true`, only apmac is supported right now. This is the name WLAN should use for wxtunnel_remote_id|
|» » comment|body|string|false|optional, user-specified string for display purpose|
|» » enable_cookie|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » ethertype|body|string|false|none|
|» » local_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » pseudo_802.1ad_enabled|body|boolean|false|optional. Enables the pseudo 802.1ad QinQ mode where the AP device drops the outer vlan tag (QinQ). This mode is useful when tunneling Mist AP’s to some aggregation routers.|
|» » remote_id|body|string|false|remote-id of the session, has to be unique in the same tunnel|
|» » remote_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » use_ap_as_session_ids|body|boolean|false|whether to use AP (last 4 bytes of MAC currently) as session ids|
|» udp_port|body|integer|false|udp port if `use_udp`==`true`|
|» use_udp|body|boolean|false|whether to use UDP instead of IP (proto=115, which is default of L2TPv3)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » ethertype|ethernet|
|» » ethertype|vlan|

|» » host_routes|body|[string]|false|optional; list of IPv4 DMVPN peer host ip-addresses to which traffic is forwarded|
|» for_mgmt|body|boolean|false|determined during creation time and cannot be toggled. A management tunnel cannot be used by wxlan rule or by wlan|
|» hello_interval|body|integer|false|in seconds, used as heartbeat to detect if a tunnel is alive. AP will try another peer after missing N hellos specified by hello_retries.|
|» hello_retries|body|integer|false|none|
|» hostname|body|string|false|optional, overwrite the hostname in SCCRQ control message, default is “” or null, %H and %M can be used, which will be replace with corresponding values:<br>* %H: name of the ap if provided (and will be stripped so it can be used for hostname) and fallbacks to MAC<br>* %M: MAC (e.g. 5c5b350e0060)|
|» ipsec|body|object|false|IPSec-related configurations; requires DMVPN be enabled|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|whether ipsec is enabled, requires DMVPN be enabled|
|» » psk|body|string|true|ipsec pre-shared key|
|» is_static|body|boolean|false|whether it’s static/unmanaged (i.e. no control session). As the session configurations are not compatible, cannot be toggled.|
|» mtu|body|integer|false|0 to enable PMTU, 552-1500 to start PMTU with a lower MTU|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the tunnel|
|» org_id|body|string(uuid)|false|none|
|» peers|body|[string]|false|list of remote peers’ IP or hostname|
|» router_id|body|string|false|optional, overwrite the router-id in SCCRQ control message, default is “0” or null, can also be an IPv4 address|
|» secret|body|string|false|secret, ‘’ if no auth is used|
|» sessions|body|[object]|false|sessions to be established with the tunnel. Has to be >= 1 in order for this tunnel to be useful. For management tunnel, it can only have 1|
|» » ap_as_session_id|body|string|false|if `use_ap_as_session_ids`==`true`, only apmac is supported right now. This is the name WLAN should use for wxtunnel_remote_id|
|» » comment|body|string|false|optional, user-specified string for display purpose|
|» » enable_cookie|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » ethertype|body|string|false|none|
|» » local_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » pseudo_802.1ad_enabled|body|boolean|false|optional. Enables the pseudo 802.1ad QinQ mode where the AP device drops the outer vlan tag (QinQ). This mode is useful when tunneling Mist AP’s to some aggregation routers.|
|» » remote_id|body|string|false|remote-id of the session, has to be unique in the same tunnel|
|» » remote_session_id|body|integer|false|1-4294967295|
|» » use_ap_as_session_ids|body|boolean|false|whether to use AP (last 4 bytes of MAC currently) as session ids|
|» udp_port|body|integer|false|udp port if `use_udp`==`true`|
|» use_udp|body|boolean|false|whether to use UDP instead of IP (proto=115, which is default of L2TPv3)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » ethertype|ethernet|
|» » ethertype|vlan|

```json
  "created_time": 0,
  "dmvpn": {
    "enabled": true,

    "host_routes": [
      "string"
    ]

  "id": "b069b358-4c97-5319-1f8c-7c5ca64d6ab1",
```

Get brief definitions of all the supported alarm types.  The example field contains an example payload as you would recieve in the alarm webhook output.

```json
      "hostnames": [

      ],

      "last_seen": 1629753888,
      "org_id": "09dac91f-6e73-4100-89f7-698e0fafbb1b",
      "severity": "warn",
      "site_id": "dcfb31a1-d615-4361-8c95-b9dde05aa704",
      "timestamp": 1629753888,
      "type": "device_down"
    },
    "fields": [
      "aps",
      "hostnames"
    ],
    "group": "infrastructure",
    "key": "device_down",
    "severity": "warn"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="getalarmdefinitions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|

<h3 id="getalarmdefinitions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» display|string|true|none|Description of the alarm type|
|» fields|[string]|true|none|List of fields available in an alarm details payload (in REST APIs & Webhooks); e.g. `aps`, `switches`, `gateways`, `hostnames`, `ssids`, `bssids`|
|» group|string|true|none|Group to which the alarm belongs|
|» key|string|true|none|Key name of an alarm type|
|» marvis_suggestion_category|string|false|none|Marvis defined category to which the alarm belongs|
