```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "new@mistsys.com"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/self/update`

Change Email
We require the user to verify that they actually own the email address they intend to change it to.

After the API call, the user will receive an email to the new email address with a link like https://manage.mist.com/verify/update?expire=:exp_time&email=:admin_email&token=:token

Upon clicking the link, the user is provided with a login page to authenticate using existing credentials. After successful login, the email address of the user gets updated

**Note**: The request parameter email can be used by UI to validate that the current session (if any) belongs to the admin or provide a login page (by pre-populating the email on login screen). UI can also use the request parameter expire to validate token expiry.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "new@mistsys.com"
}
```

<h3 id="updateselfemail-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[Model_object_email](#schemamodel_object_email)|false|Request Body|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|none|

```json
{}
```

```json
{}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ack_admin_id|string(uuid)|false|none|UUID of the admin who acked the alarm|
|ack_admin_name|string|false|none|Name & Email ID of the admin who acked the alarm|
|acked|boolean|false|none|Whether the alarm is acked or not|
|acked_time|integer|false|read-only|Epoch (seconds) when the alarm was acked|
|aps|[string]|false|none|additional information: List of MACs of the APs e.g. [“ffeeddccbbaa”, “ffeeddccbbab”]|
|bssids|[string]|false|none|List of BSSIDs|
|count|integer|true|read-only|Number of incident within an alarm window|
|gateways|[string]|false|none|additional information: List of MACs of the gateways e.g. [“ffeeddccbbaa”, “ffeeddccbbab”]|
|group|string|true|none|Group of the alarm|
|hostnames|[string]|false|none|additional information: List of Hostnames of the devices (AP/Switch/Gateway)|
|id|string(uuid)|true|read-only|UUID of the alarm|
|last_seen|integer|true|none|Epoch (seconds) of the last incident/alarm within an alarm window|
|note|string|false|none|Text describing the alarm|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|none|UUID of the org|
|severity|string|true|none|Severity of the alarm|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|UUID of the site|
|ssids|[string]|false|none|List of SSIDs|
|switches|[string]|false|none|additional information: List of MACs of the switches e.g. [“ffeeddccbbaa”, “ffeeddccbbab”]|
|timestamp|integer|true|read-only|Epoch (seconds) of the first incident/alarm|
|type|string|true|read-only|Key-name of the alarm type|


BLE AP settings

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|beacon_enabled|boolean|false|none|whether Mist beacons is enabled|
|beacon_rate|integer|false|none|required if `beacon_rate_mode`==`custom`, 1-10, in number-beacons-per-second|
|beacon_rate_mode|string|false|none|none|
|beam_disabled|[integer]|false|none|list of AP BLE location beam numbers (1-8) which should be disabled at the AP and not transmit location information (where beam 1 is oriented at the top the AP, growing counter-clock-wise, with 9 being the omni BLE beam)|
|eddystone_uid_adv_power|integer|false|none|advertised TX Power, -100 to 20 (dBm), omit this attribute to use default|
|eddystone_uid_beams|string|false|none|none|
|eddystone_uid_enabled|boolean|false|none|only if `beacon_enabled`==`false`, Whether Eddystone-UID beacon is enabled|
|eddystone_uid_freq_msec|integer|false|none|Frequency (msec) of data emmit by Eddystone-UID beacon|
|eddystone_uid_instance|string|false|none|Eddystone-UID instance for the device|
|eddystone_uid_namespace|string|false|none|Eddystone-UID namespace|
|eddystone_url_adv_power|integer|false|none|advertised TX Power, -100 to 20 (dBm), omit this attribute to use default|
|eddystone_url_beams|string|false|none|none|
|eddystone_url_enabled|boolean|false|none|only if `beacon_enabled`==`false`, Whether Eddystone-URL beacon is enabled|
|eddystone_url_freq_msec|integer|false|none|Frequency (msec) of data emmit by Eddystone-UID beacon|
|eddystone_url_url|string|false|none|URL pointed by Eddystone-URL beacon|
|ibeacon_adv_power|integer|false|none|advertised TX Power, -100 to 20 (dBm), omit this attribute to use default|
|ibeacon_beams|string|false|none|none|
|ibeacon_enabled|boolean|false|none|can be enabled if `beacon_enabled`==`true`, whether to send iBeacon|
|ibeacon_freq_msec|integer|false|none|Frequency (msec) of data emmit for iBeacon|
|ibeacon_major|integer|false|none|Major number for iBeacon|
|ibeacon_minor|integer|false|none|Minor number for iBeacon|
|ibeacon_uuid|string(uuid)|false|none|optional, if not specified, the same UUID as the beacon will be used|
|power|integer|false|none|required if `power_mode`==`custom`|
|power_mode|string|false|none|default / custom|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|beacon_rate_mode|default|
|beacon_rate_mode|custom|

|name|string|false|none|none|
|notes|string|false|none|any notes about this AP|
|ntp_servers|[string]|false|none|none|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|orientation|number|false|none|orientation, 0-359, in degrees, up is 0, right is 90.|

|radio_config|[ap_radio](#schemaap_radio)|false|none|Radio AP settings|

|uplink_port_config|object|false|none|none|
|usb_config|[ap_usb](#schemaap_usb)|false|none|USB AP settings|
|vars|object|false|none|a dictionary of name->value, the vars can then be used in Wlans. This can overwrite those from Site Vars|
|x|number|false|none|x in pixel|
|y|number|false|none|y in pixel|

Switch Configuration
You can configure `port_usages` and `networks` settings at the device level, but most of the time it's better use the Site Setting to achieve better consistency and be able to re-use the same settings across switches entries defined here will "replace" those defined in Site Setting/Network Template

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acl_policies|[[junos_acl_policies](#schemajunos_acl_policies)]|false|none|none|
|acl_tags|object|false|none|ACL Tags to identify traffic source or destination. Key name is the tag name|
|additional_config_cmds|[string]|false|none|none|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|deviceprofile_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|dhcp_config|[junos_dhcpd](#schemajunos_dhcpd)|false|none|if DHCP Server/Relay is intended. The property key is the network name|
|dhcp_snooping|[junos_dhcp_snooping](#schemajunos_dhcp_snooping)|false|none|none|
|disable_auto_config|boolean|false|none|for a claimed switch, we control the configs by default. This option (disables the behavior)|
|dns_servers|[string]|false|none|Global dns settings. To keep compatibility, dns settings in `ip_config` and `oob_ip_config` will overwrite this setting|
|dns_suffix|[string]|false|none|Global dns settings. To keep compatibility, dns settings in `ip_config` and `oob_ip_config` will overwrite this setting|
|evpn_config|[junos_evpn_config](#schemajunos_evpn_config)|false|none|EVPN Junos settings|
|extra_routes|object|false|none|The property key is the network name or a CIDR|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|image1_url|string \| null|false|none|none|
|image2_url|string \| null|false|none|none|
|image3_url|string \| null|false|none|none|
|ip_config|[junos_ip_config](#schemajunos_ip_config)|false|none|Junos IP Config|
|managed|boolean|false|none|for an adopted switch, we don’t overwrite their existing configs automatically|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|networks|[junos_networks](#schemajunos_networks)|false|none|A network represents a network segment. It can either represent a VLAN (then usually ties to a L3 subnet), optionally associate it with a subnet which can later be used to create addition routes. Used for ports doing `family ethernet-switching`. It can also be a pure L3-subnet that can then be used against a port that with `family inet`.|
|notes|string|false|none|none|
|ntp_servers|[string]|false|none|list of NTP servers specific to this device. By default, those in Site Settings will be used|
|oob_ip_config|[junos_oob_ip_config](#schemajunos_oob_ip_config)|false|none|Junos out-of-band (vme/em0/fxp0) IP config|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|ospf_config|[junos_ospf_config](#schemajunos_ospf_config)|false|none|Junos OSPF config|
|other_ip_configs|object|false|none|The property key is the network name|
|port_config|object|false|none|The property key is the port name or range (e.g. "ge-0/0/0-10")|
|port_mirroring|object|false|none|none|
|port_usages|object|false|none|The property key is the port profile name|
|radius_config|[junos_radius_config](#schemajunos_radius_config)|false|none|Junos Radius config|
|role|string|false|none|none|
|router_id|string|false|none|used for OSPF / BGP / EVPN|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|vars|object|false|none|a dictionary of name->value, the vars can then be used in Wlans. This can overwrite those from Site Vars|
|virtual_chassis|object|false|none|required for preprovisioned Virtual Chassis|
|vrf_config|[junos_vrf_config](#schemajunos_vrf_config)|false|none|none|
|vrrp_config|[junos_vrrp_config](#schemajunos_vrrp_config)|false|none|Junos VRRP config|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|role|access|
|role|aggregation|

<h2 id="tocS_device_upgrade">device_upgrade</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadevice_upgrade"></a>
<a id="schema_device_upgrade"></a>
<a id="tocSdevice_upgrade"></a>
<a id="tocsdevice_upgrade"></a>

```json
{
  "canary_phases": [
    1,
    10,
    50,
    100
  ],
  "device_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "enable_p2p": true,
  "force": false,
  "max_failure_percentage": 5,
  "max_failures": [
    0
  ],
  "models": [
    "string"
  ],
  "p2p_cluster_size": 0,
  "p2p_parallelism": 0,
  "reboot": false,
  "reboot_at": 1624399840,
  "rrm_first_batch_percentage": 2,
  "rrm_max_batch_percentage": 10,
  "rrm_mesh_upgrade": "string",
  "rrm_node_order": "fringe_to_center",
  "rrm_slow_ramp": true,
  "snapshot": false,
  "start_time": 1624399840,
  "strategy": "big_bang",
  "version": "3.1.5"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|canary_phases|[integer]|false|none|phases for canary deployment. Each phase represents percentage of AP’s that need to be upgraded. default is [1, 10, 50, 100]|
|device_ids|[string]|false|none|none|
|enable_p2p|boolean|false|none|whether to allow local AP-to-AP FW upgrade|
|force|boolean|false|none|true will force upgrade when requested version is same as running version|
|max_failure_percentage|number|false|none|percentage of failures allowed across the entire upgrade(not applicable for `big_bang`)|
|max_failures|[integer]|false|none|number of failures allowed within each phase(applicable for `canary` or `rrm`). Will be used if provided, else max_failure_percentage will be used|
|models|[string]|false|none|none|
|p2p_cluster_size|integer|false|none|none|
|p2p_parallelism|integer|false|none|number of parallel p2p download batches to creat|
|reboot|boolean|false|none|Reboot device immediately after upgrade is completed (Available on Junos OS devices)|
|reboot_at|number|false|none|reboot start time in epoch seconds, default is `start_time`|
|rrm_first_batch_percentage|integer|false|none|percentage of AP’s that need to be present in the first rrm batch|
|rrm_max_batch_percentage|integer|false|none|max percentage of AP’s that need to be present in each rrm batch|
|rrm_mesh_upgrade|string|false|none|sequential or parallel (default parallel). Whether to upgrade mesh AP’s parallelly or sequentially at the end of the upgrade|
|rrm_node_order|string|false|none|Used in rrm to determine whether to start upgrade from fringe or center AP’s|
|rrm_slow_ramp|boolean|false|none|true will make rrm batch sizes slowly ramp up|
|snapshot|boolean|false|none|Perform recovery snapshot after device is rebooted (Available on Junos OS devices)|
|start_time|number|false|none|upgrade start time in epoch seconds, default is now|
|strategy|string|false|none|`big_bang` (upgrade all at once), `serial` (one at a time), `canary` or `rrm`|
|version|string|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rrm_node_order|fringe_to_center|
|rrm_node_order|center_to_fringe|
|strategy|big_bang|
|strategy|canary|
|strategy|serial|
|strategy|rrm|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|counts|object|false|read-only|none|
|current_phase|integer|false|none|current canary or rrm phase in progress|
|enable_p2p|boolean|false|none|whether to allow local AP-to-AP FW upgrade|
|force|boolean|false|none|whether to force upgrade when requested version is same as running version|
|id|string(uuid)|true|read-only|unique id for the upgrade|
|max_failure_percentage|integer|false|none|percentage of failures allowed|
|max_failures|[integer]|false|none|number of failures allowed within a canary phase or serial rollout|
|reboot_at|integer|false|none|reboot start time in epoch|
|start_time|number|false|none|firmware download start time in epoch|
|status|string|false|none|status upgrade is in|
|strategy|string|false|none|upgrade strategy|
|target_version|string|false|none|version to upgrade to|
|upgrade_plan|object|false|none|a dictionary of rrm phase number to devices part of that phase|

|---|---|

|status|completed|
|status|canceled|
|status|downloading|
|strategy|big_bang|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aeroscout|[ap_aeroscout](#schemaap_aeroscout)|false|none|Aeroscout AP settings|
|ble_config|[ap_ble](#schemaap_ble)|false|none|BLE AP settings|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|disable_eth1|boolean|false|none|whether to disable eth1 port|
|disable_eth2|boolean|false|none|whether to disable eth2 port|
|disable_eth3|boolean|false|none|whether to disable eth3 port|
|disable_module|boolean|false|none|whether to disable module port|
|for_site|boolean|false|read-only|none|
|height|number \| null|false|none|Device Only. Height, in meters, optional|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|iot_config|[ap_iot](#schemaap_iot)|false|none|IoT AP settings|
|ip_config|[ap_ip](#schemaap_ip)|false|none|IP AP settings|
|led|[ap_led](#schemaap_led)|false|none|LED AP settings|
|map_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Device Only.. Map where the device belongs to|
|mesh|[ap_mesh](#schemaap_mesh)|false|none|Mesh AP settings|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|name|string \| null|false|none|none|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Device Only. Any notes about this AP|
|ntp_servers|[string]|false|none|none|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|orientation|number|false|none|Device Only. Orientation, 0-359, in degrees, up is 0, right is 90.|
|orientation_overwrite|boolean|false|none|whether the user overwrite the orientation|
|poe_passthrough|boolean|false|none|whether to enable power out through module port (for APH) or eth1 (for APL/BT11)|
|port_config|object|false|none|The property key is the interface(s) name (e.g. "eth1,eth2")|
|pwr_config|object|false|none|power related configs|
|radio_config|[ap_radio](#schemaap_radio)|false|none|Radio AP settings|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|switch_config|[ap_switch](#schemaap_switch)|false|none|**Deprecated.** for people who want to fully control the vlans (advanced)|
|type|string|false|none|none|
|usb_config|[ap_usb](#schemaap_usb)|false|none|USB AP settings|
|vars|object|false|none|a dictionary of name->value, the vars can then be used in Wlans. This can overwrite those from Site Vars|
|x|number \| null|false|none|Device Only. x in pixel|
|y|number \| null|false|none|Device Only. y in pixel|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|ap|
|type|switch|
|type|gateway|

|deny_dst_tags|[string]|false|none|- for GBP-based policy, all src_tags and dst_tags have to be gbp-based<br>- for ACL-based policy, `network` is required in either the source or destination so that we know where to attach the policy to|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|src_tags|[string]|false|none|none|

|macs|[string]|false|none|required if <br>- `type`==`mac`<br>- `type`==`static_gbp` if from matching mac|
|network|string|false|none|if:<br>- `type`==`mac` (optional. default is `any`)<br>- `type`==`subnet` (optional. default is `any`)<br>- `type`==`network`<br>- `type`==`resource` (optional. default is `any`)<br>- `type`==`static_gbp` if from matching network (vlan)|
|radius_group|string|false|none|required if <br>- `type`==`radius_group` <br>- `type`==`static_gbp` if from matching radius_group|
|specs|[object]|false|none|if `type`==`resource`<br>empty means unrestricted, i.e. any|
|subnets|[string]|false|none|if <br>- `type`==`subnet` <br>- `type`==`resource` (optional. default is `any`)<br>- `type`==`static_gbp` if from matching subnet|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|mac|
|type|subnet|
|type|network|
|type|radius_group|
|type|any|
|type|resource|
|type|dynamic_gbp|
|type|static_gbp|

<h2 id="tocS_junos_networks">junos_networks</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajunos_networks"></a>
<a id="schema_junos_networks"></a>
<a id="tocSjunos_networks"></a>
<a id="tocsjunos_networks"></a>

```json
{
  "dns": [
    "string"
  ],
  "dns_suffix": [
    "string"
  ],
  "gateway": "string",
  "ospf_interface_type": "string",
  "subnet": "string",
  "vlan_id": 0,
  "zone": "string"
}
```

A network represents a network segment. It can either represent a VLAN (then usually ties to a L3 subnet), optionally associate it with a subnet which can later be used to create addition routes. Used for ports doing `family ethernet-switching`. It can also be a pure L3-subnet that can then be used against a port that with `family inet`.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|dns_suffix|[string]|false|none|none|
|gateway|string|false|none|none|
|ospf_interface_type|string|false|none|none|
|subnet|string|false|none|optional for pure switching, required when L3 / routing features are used|
|vlan_id|integer|true|none|none|
|zone|string|false|none|used for gateway|

```json
{
  "all_networks": false,
  "allow_dhcpd": true,
  "bypass_auth_when_server_down": true,
  "description": "string",
  "disable_autoneg": false,
  "disabled": false,
  "duplex": "auto",
  "enable_mac_auth": true,
  "enable_qos": true,
  "guest_network": "string",
  "mac_auth_only": true,
  "mac_limit": 0,
  "mode": "access",
  "mtu": 0,
  "networks": [
    "string"
  ],
  "persist_mac": false,
  "poe_disabled": false,
  "port_auth": "string",
  "port_network": "string",
  "rejected_network": true,
  "speed": "string",
  "storm_control": {
    "no_broadcast": false,
    "no_multicast": false,
    "no_registered_multicast": false,
    "no_unknown_unicast": false,
    "percentage": 80
  },
  "stp_edge": true,
  "voip_network": "string"
}
```

Junos port usages

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|all_networks|boolean|false|none|if `mode`==`trunk`, whether to trunk all network/vlans|
|allow_dhcpd|boolean|false|none|if DHCP snooping is enabled, whether DHCP server is allowed on the interfaces with. All the interfaces from port configs using this port usage are effected. Please notice that allow_dhcpd is a tri-state.<br><br>When it is not defined, it means using the system’s default setting which depends on whether the port is a access or trunk port.|
|bypass_auth_when_server_down|boolean|false|none|if `port_auth`==`dot1x`, whether to allow the device to connect if RADIUS server is down|
|description|string|false|none|description|
|disable_autoneg|boolean|false|none|if speed and duplex are specified, whether to disable autonegotiation|
|disabled|boolean|false|none|whether the port is disabled|
|duplex|string|false|none|link connection mode, choices are auto (default), full, and half|
|enable_mac_auth|boolean|false|none|if `port_auth`==`dot1x`, whether to enable MAC Auth|
|enable_qos|boolean|false|none|none|
|guest_network|string|false|none|if `port_auth`==`dot1x`, which network to put the device into if the device cannot do dot1x. default is null (i.e. not allowed)|
|mac_auth_only|boolean|false|none|only effect once `enable_mac_auth`==`true`|
|mac_limit|integer|false|none|max number of mac addresses, default is 0 for unlimited, otherwise range is 1 or higher, with upper bound constrained by platform|
|mode|string|false|none|access (default) / trunk|
|mtu|integer|false|none|media maximum transmission unit (MTU) is the largest data unit that can be forwarded without fragmentation. The default value is 1514.|
|networks|[string]|false|none|if `mode`==`trunk`, the list of network/vlans|
|persist_mac|boolean|false|none|if `mode`==`access` and `port_auth`!=`dot1x`, whether the port should retain dynamically learned MAC addresses|
|poe_disabled|boolean|false|none|whether PoE capabilities are disabled for a port|
|port_auth|string|false|none|if dot1x is desired, set to dot1x|
|port_network|string|false|none|native network/vlan for untagged traffic|
|rejected_network|boolean|false|none|if `port_auth`==`dot1x`, when radius server reject / fails|
|speed|string|false|none|speed, default is auto to automatically negotiate speed|
|storm_control|[junos_storm_control](#schemajunos_storm_control)|false|none|Switch storm control|
|stp_edge|boolean|false|none|when enabled, the port is not expected to receive BPDU frames|
|voip_network|string|false|none|network/vlan for voip traffic, must also set port_network. to authenticate device, set port_auth|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|duplex|half|
|duplex|full|
|duplex|auto|
|mode|access|
|mode|trunk|
|mode|inet|
|mode|wan|

<h2 id="tocS_junos_port_usages_dynamic">junos_port_usages_dynamic</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajunos_port_usages_dynamic"></a>
<a id="schema_junos_port_usages_dynamic"></a>
<a id="tocSjunos_port_usages_dynamic"></a>
<a id="tocsjunos_port_usages_dynamic"></a>

```json
{
  "mode": "dynamic",
  "reset_default_when": "link_down",
  "rules": [
    {
      "equals": "string",
      "equals_any": [
        "string"
      ],
      "expression": "string",
      "src": "lldp_chassis_id",
      "usage": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

This is a special mode where the actually usage is determined by a set of rules the port will start with `access` mode and isolated depending on the rules, if resolved, the port will have the resolved usage applied.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mode|string|true|none|none|
|reset_default_when|string|false|none|Control when the DPC port should be changed to the default port usage<br>Configuring to none will let the DPC port keep at the current port usage.|
|rules|[object]|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|dynamic|
|reset_default_when|none|
|reset_default_when|link_down|

|auth_servers_timeout|integer|false|none|radius auth session timeout|
|coa_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|coa_port|integer|false|none|none|
|network|string|false|none|use `network`or `source_ip`<br>which network the RADIUS server resides, if there's static IP for this network, we'd use it as source-ip|
|source_ip|string|false|none|use `network`or `source_ip`|

MxEdge Radsec Configuration

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acct_servers|[object]|false|none|list of RADIUS accounting servers, optional, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|auth_servers|[object]|false|none|list of RADIUS authentication servers, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|whether to enable service on Mist Edge i.e. RADIUS proxy over TLS|
|match_ssid|boolean|false|none|whether to match ssid in request message to select from a subset of RADIUS servers|
|proxy_hosts|[string]|false|none|hostnames or IPs for Mist AP to use as the TLS Server (i.e. they are reachable from AP) in addition to `tunterm_hosts`|
|server_selection|string|false|none|ordered (default) / unordered. When ordered, Mist Edge will prefer and go back to the first radius server if possible|
|source|string|false|none|Specify source address to use when connecting to RADIUS servers|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|server_selection|ordered|
|server_selection|unordered|
|source|tunnel|
|source|oob|
|source|any|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|anchor_mxtunnel_ids|[string(uuid)]|false|none|list of anchor mxtunnels used for forming edge to edge tunnels|
|auto_preemption|object|false|none|none|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|for_site|boolean|false|read-only|none|
|hello_interval|integer \| null|false|none|in seconds, used as heartbeat to detect if a tunnel is alive. AP will try another peer after missing N hellos specified by `hello_retries`.|
|hello_retries|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|ipsec|object|false|none|none|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|mtu|integer|false|none|0 to enable PMTU, 552-1500 to start PMTU with a lower MTU|
|mxcluster_ids|[string(uuid)]|false|none|list of mxclusters to deploy this tunnel to|
|name|string \| null|false|none|none|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|protocol|string|false|none|none|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|

Networks are usually subnets that have cross-site significance. `networks`in Org Settings will got merged into `networks`in Site Setting. For gateways, they can be used to define Service Routes.

|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|internal_access|object|false|none|none|
|internet_access|object|false|none|whether this network has direct internet access|
|isolation|boolean|false|none|whether to allow clients in the network to talk to each other|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|subnet|string|false|none|none|
|tenants|object|false|none|none|
|vlan_id|integer|false|none|none|
|vpn_access|object|false|none|whether this network can be accessed from vpn|

Security Policy is designed to audit / catch discripancies between “what’s intended to be running” versus “what’s actually running” in a network. Many big organizations have separated Security and IT team (for good reasons). Each site can be assigned a security policy. Whenever an AP is provisioned, the configuration will be checked against the security policy. Any violations will be flagged in Device Config History where you can search for the when and where the violation occurs.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|wlans|[[wlan](#schemawlan)]|false|none|none|

```json
  },
```

```json
    "bounce": "string",
    "engaged": "string",

  },

    "fri": "string",
    "mon": "string",

    "sun": "string",

    "tue": "string",
    "wed": "string"
  },
  "max_dwell": 43200,
  "min_dwell": 0
}
```

**Note**: if hours does not exist, it’s treated as everyday of the week, 00:00-23:59. Currently we don’t allow multiple ranges for the same day

**Note**: default values for `dwell_tags`: passerby (1,300) bounce (301, 14400) engaged (14401, 28800) stationed (28801, 42000)

**Note**: default values for `dwell_tag_names`: passerby = “Passerby”, bounce = “Visitor”, engaged = “Associates”, stationed = “Assets”

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dwell_tag_names|object|true|none|none|
|dwell_tags|object|false|none|add tags to visits within the duration (in seconds), available tags (passerby, bounce, engaged, stationed)|
|hours|object|false|none|hours of operation filter, the available days (mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun). <br><br>**Note**: If the dow is not defined then it’s treated as 00:00-23:59.|
|max_dwell|integer|false|none|max time, default is 43200(12h), max is 68400 (18h)|
|min_dwell|integer|false|none|min time|

|---|---|---|---|---|

|clusters|[object]|false|none|for AP, how to connect to tunterm or radsecproxy|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|for_site|boolean|false|read-only|none|
|hello_interval|integer|false|none|in seconds, used as heartbeat to detect if a tunnel is alive. AP will try another peer after missing N hellos specified by hello_retries|
|hello_retries|integer|false|none|none|
|hosts|[string]|false|none|hostnames or IPs where a Mist Tunnel will use as the Peer (i.e. they are reachable from AP)|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|mtu|integer|false|none|0 to enable PMTU, 552-1500 to start PMTU with a lower MTU|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|protocol|string|false|none|none|
|radsec|object|false|none|none|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|vlan_ids|[integer \| string]|false|none|list of vlan_ids that will be use|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|protocol|udp|
|protocol|ip|

<h2 id="tocS_site_occupancy_analytics">site_occupancy_analytics</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasite_occupancy_analytics"></a>
<a id="schema_site_occupancy_analytics"></a>
<a id="tocSsite_occupancy_analytics"></a>
<a id="tocssite_occupancy_analytics"></a>

```json
{
  "assets_enabled": false,
  "clients_enabled": true,
  "min_duration": 3000,
  "sdkclients_enabled": false,
  "unconnected_clients_enabled": false
}
```

Occupancy Analytics settings

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|assets_enabled|boolean|false|none|indicate whether named BLE assets should be included in the zone occupancy calculation|
|clients_enabled|boolean|false|none|indicate whether connected WiFi clients should be included in the zone occupancy calculation|
|min_duration|integer|false|none|minimum duration|
|sdkclients_enabled|boolean|false|none|indicate whether SDK clients should be included in the zone occupancy calculation|
|unconnected_clients_enabled|boolean|false|none|indicate whether unconnected WiFi clients should be included in the zone occupancy calculation|

<h2 id="tocS_site_rogue">site_rogue</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasite_rogue"></a>
<a id="schema_site_rogue"></a>
<a id="tocSsite_rogue"></a>
<a id="tocssite_rogue"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "honeypot_enabled": true,
  "min_duration": 10,
  "min_rssi": -80,
  "whitelisted_bssids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "whitelisted_ssids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Rogue site settings

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|whether or not rogue detection is enabled|
|honeypot_enabled|boolean|false|none|whether or not honeypot detection is enabled|
|min_duration|integer|false|none|minimum duration for a bssid to be considered rogue|
|min_rssi|integer|false|none|minimum RSSI for an AP to be considered rogue (ignoring APs that’s far away)|
|whitelisted_bssids|[string]|false|none|list of BSSIDs to whitelist. Ex: "cc-:8e-:6f-:d4-:bf-:16", "cc-8e-6f-d4-bf-16", "cc-73-*", "cc:82:*"|
|whitelisted_ssids|[string]|false|none|list of SSIDs to whitelist|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|ap_port_config|object|false|none|none|

|auto_upgrade|[site_auto_upgrade](#schemasite_auto_upgrade)|false|none|Auto Upgrade Settings|
|blacklist_url|string|false|read-only|none|
|ble_config|[ap_ble](#schemaap_ble)|false|none|BLE AP settings|
|config_auto_revert|boolean|false|none|whether to enable ap auto config revert|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|device_updown_threshold|integer|false|none|sending AP_DISCONNECTED event in device-updowns only if AP_CONNECTED is not seen within the threshold, in minutes|
|dns_servers|[string]|false|none|list of NTP servers|
|dns_suffix|[string]|false|none|list of NTP servers|
|enable_channel_144|boolean|false|none|whether to enable channel 144 (some older clients may not support it)|
|engagement|[site_engagement](#schemasite_engagement)|false|none|**Note**: if hours does not exist, it’s treated as everyday of the week, 00:00-23:59. Currently we don’t allow multiple ranges for the same day<br><br>**Note**: default values for `dwell_tags`: passerby (1,300) bounce (301, 14400) engaged (14401, 28800) stationed (28801, 42000)<br><br>**Note**: default values for `dwell_tag_names`: passerby = “Passerby”, bounce = “Visitor”, engaged = “Associates”, stationed = “Assets”|
|evpn_options|[junos_evpn_options](#schemajunos_evpn_options)|false|none|EVPN Options|
|flags|object|false|none|name/val pair objects for location engine to use|
|for_site|boolean|false|read-only|none|
|gateway_additional_config_cmds|[string]|false|none|additional CLI commands to append to the generated config for gateways<br><br>**Note**: no check is done|
|gateway_mgmt|[site_gateway](#schemasite_gateway)|false|none|Gateway Site settings|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|led|[ap_led](#schemaap_led)|false|none|LED AP settings|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|mxedge|object|false|none|site mist edges form a cluster of radsecproxy servers|
|mxedge_mgmt|[mxedge_mgmt](#schemamxedge_mgmt)|false|none|none|
|mxtunnels|[site_mxtunnel](#schemasite_mxtunnel)|false|none|Site MxTunnel|
|networks|object|false|none|the property key is the network name|
|ntp_servers|[string]|false|none|list of NTP servers|
|occupancy|[site_occupancy_analytics](#schemasite_occupancy_analytics)|false|none|Occupancy Analytics settings|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|ospf_areas|object|false|none|the property key is the OSPF area|
|persist_config_on_device|boolean|false|none|whether to store the config on AP|
|port_usages|object|false|none|the property key is the port usage name|
|proxy|object|false|none|Proxy Configuration for APs and Site Edges to talk to Mist|
|radio_config|[ap_radio](#schemaap_radio)|false|none|Radio AP settings|
|radius_config|[junos_radius_config](#schemajunos_radius_config)|false|none|Junos Radius config|
|remote_syslog|[remote_syslog](#schemaremote_syslog)|false|none|none|
|report_gatt|boolean|false|none|whether AP should periodically connect to BLE devices and report GATT device info (device name, manufacturer name, serial number, battery %, temperature, humidity)|
|rogue|[site_rogue](#schemasite_rogue)|false|none|Rogue site settings|

|cisco_enabled|boolean|false|none|none|
|disable_11k|boolean|false|none|whether to disable 11k|
|disable_radios_when_power_constrained|boolean|false|none|none|
|enable_arp_spoof_check|boolean|false|none|when proxy_arp is enabled, check for arp spoofing.|
|enable_channel_144|boolean|false|none|whether to enable channel 144 (some older clients may not support it)|
|enable_shared_radio_scanning|boolean|false|none|none|
|enable_vna|boolean|false|none|enable Virtual Network Assistant (using SUB-VNA license)|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|enable WIFI feature (using SUB-MAN license)|
|locate_connected|boolean|false|none|whether to locate connected clients|
|locate_unconnected|boolean|false|none|whether to locate unconnected clients|
|mesh_allow_dfs|boolean|false|none|whether to allow Mesh to use DFS channels. For DFS channels, Remote Mesh AP would have to do CAC when scanning for new Base AP, which is slow and will distrupt the connection. If roaming is desired, keep it disabled.|
|mesh_enable_crm|boolean|false|none|used to enable/disable CRM|
|mesh_enabled|boolean|false|none|whether to enable Mesh feature for the site|
|mesh_psk|string|false|none|optional passphrase of mesh networking, default is generated randomly|
|mesh_ssid|string|false|none|optional ssid of mesh networking, default is based on site_id|
|proxy_arp|string|false|none|default / enabled / disabled|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|proxy_arp|default|
|proxy_arp|enabled|
|proxy_arp|disabled|

SSO

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|custom_logout_url|string|false|none|optional, a URL we will redirect the user after user logout from Mist (for some IdP which supports a custom logout URL that is different from SP-initiated SLO process)|
|default_role|string|false|none|default role to assign if there’s no match. By default, an assertion is treated as invalid when there’s no role matched|
|domain|string|false|none|none|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|idp_cert|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`saml`. IDP Cert (used to verify the signed response)|
|idp_sign_algo|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`saml`. Signing algorithm for SAML Assertion|

|idp_type|string|false|none|none|

|issuer|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`saml`. IDP issuer URL|

|ldap_certs|[string]|false|none|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|ldap_client_cert|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|ldap_client_key|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|ldap_group_attr|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|ldap_group_dn|string|false|none|if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|ldap_group_filter|string|false|none|if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|ldap_server_hosts|[string]|false|none|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|ldap_type|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`ldap`|
|ldap_user_filter|string|false|none|* if `ldap_type`==`ad`: "(CN=%s)"<br>* if `ldap_type`==`okta`: "(uid=%s)"<br>* if `ldap_type`==`custom`|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|msp_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|name|string|true|none|name|
|nameid_format|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`saml`|
|oauth_cc_client_id|string|false|none|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, Client Credentials|
|oauth_cc_client_secret|string|false|none|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, oauth_cc_client_secret is RSA private key, of the form "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY--...."|
|oauth_discovery_url|string|false|none|if `idp_type`==`oauth`|
|oauth_ropc_client_id|string|false|none|ropc = Resource Owner Password Credentials|
|oauth_ropc_secret|string|false|none|oauth_ropc_client_secret can be empty if oauth_type is azure|
|oauth_tenant_id|string|false|none|if `oauth_type`==`okta`, oauth_tenant_id|
|oauth_type|string|false|none|none|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|role_attr_extraction|string|false|none|optional, custom role attribute parsing scheme<br><br>Supported Role Parsing Schemes<br><table><tr><th>Name</th><th>Scheme</th></tr><tr><td>cn</td><td><ul><li>The expected role attribute format in SAML Assertion is “CN=cn,OU=ou1,OU=ou2,…”</li><li>CN (the key) is case insensitive and exactly 1 CN is expected (or the entire entry will be ignored)</li><li>E.g. if role attribute is “CN=cn,OU=ou1,OU=ou2” then parsed role value is “cn”</li></ul></td></tr></table>|
|role_attr_from|string|false|none| name of the attribute in SAML Assertion to extract role from|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|type|string|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_ttl|number|true|none|TTL of the validity of the stat|
|accuracy|integer|false|none|estimated clinet location accuracy, in meter|

|ap_id|string(uuid)|true|none|AP ID the client is connected to|
|ap_mac|string|true|none|AP the client is connected to|
|band|string|true|none|none|
|channel|integer|true|none|current channel|
|dual_band|boolean|true|none|whether the client is dual-band capable (determined by whether we’ve seen probe requests from both bands)|
|family|string|true|none|device family, through fingerprinting. iPod / Nexus Galaxy / Windows Mobile or CE …|
|guest|object|false|none|information about this portal|
|hostname|string|true|none|hostname that we learned from sniffing DHCP|
|idle_time|number|true|none|how long, in seconds, has the client been idle (since the last RX packet)|
|ip|string(ipv4)|true|none|none|
|ip6|string(ipv6)|false|none|none|
|is_guest|boolean|true|none|whether this is a guest|
|key_mgmt|string|true|none|e.g. WPA2-PSK/CCMP|
|last_seen|number|true|none|last seen timestamp|
|mac|string|true|none|client mac|
|manufacture|string|true|none|device manufacture, through fingerprinting or OUI|
|map_id|string(uuid)|false|none|estimated client location - map_id|
|model|string|true|none|device model, may be available if we can identify them|
|num_locating_aps|integer|false|none|number of APs used to locate this client|
|os|string|true|none|device os, through fingerprinting|
|power_saving|boolean|true|none|if it’s currently in power-save mode|
|proto|string|true|none|none|
|psk_id|string(uuid)|false|none|PSK id (if multi-psk is used)|
|rssi|number|true|none|signal strength|
|rx_bps|number|true|none|rate of receiving traffic from the clients, bits/seconds, last known|
|rx_bytes|number|true|none|amount of traffic received from client since client connects|
|rx_packets|number|true|none|amount of traffic received from client since client connects|
|rx_rate|number|true|none|RX Rate, Mbps|
|rx_retries|number|true|none|amount of rx retries|
|snr|number|true|none|signal over noise|
|ssid|string|true|none|SSID the client is connected to|
|tx_bps|number|true|none|rate of transmitting traffic to the clients, bits/seconds, last known|
|tx_bytes|number|true|none|amount of traffic sent to client since client connects|
|tx_packets|number|true|none|amount of traffic sent to client since client connects|
|tx_rate|number|true|none|TX Rate, Mbps|
|tx_retries|number|true|none|amount of tx retries|
|type|string|false|none|client’s type, regular / vip / resource / blocked (if client object is created)|
|uptime|number|true|none|how long, in seconds, has the client been connected|
|username|string|true|none|username that we learned from 802.1X exchange or Per-user PSK or User Portal|
|vlan_id|integer|false|none|vlan id, could be empty (from older AP)|
|wlan_id|string(uuid)|true|none|WLAN ID the client is connected to|
|x|number|false|none|estimated client location in pixels|
|x_m|number|false|none|estimated client location in meter|
|y|number|false|none|estimated client location in pixels|
|y_m|number|false|none|estimated client location in meter|

|band|5|
|proto|a|
|proto|b|
|proto|g|
|proto|n|
|proto|ac|
|proto|ax|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|cert_expiry|number|false|none|none|
|env_stat|object|false|none|device environment, including CPU temperature, Ambient temperature, Humidity, Attitude, Pressure, Accelerometers, Magnetometers and vCore Voltage|
|ext_ip|string|false|none|none|
|fwupdate|object|false|none|none|
|iot_stat|object|false|none|none|
|ip|string|false|none|none|
|ip_config|object|false|none|none|
|ip_stat|object|false|none|none|
|l2tp_stat|object|false|none|l2tp tunnel status (key is the wxtunnel_id)|
|last_seen|number|false|none|last seen timestamp|
|last_trouble|object|false|none|none|
|led|object|false|none|none|
|lldp_stat|object|false|none|LLDP Stat (neighbor information, power negotiations)|
|locating|boolean|false|none|none|
|locked|boolean|false|none|whether this AP is considered locked (placement / orientation has been vetted)|
|mac|string|true|none|device mac|
|map_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|mesh_downlinks|object|false|none|none|
|mesh_uplink|object|false|none|none|
|model|string|true|none|device model|
|mount|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|none|
|num_clients|integer|false|none|how many wireless clients are currently connected|
|port_stat|object|false|none|none|
|power_budget|number|false|none|in mW, surplus if positie or deficit if negative|
|power_src|string|false|none|DC Input / PoE 802.3at / PoE 802.3af / LLDP / ? (unknown)|
|radio_config|object|false|none|none|
|radio_stat|object|false|none|a map of radio stats, key can be band_24 / band_5|
|rx_bps|number|false|none|none|
|rx_bytes|integer|false|none|none|
|rx_pkts|integer|false|none|none|
|serial|string|false|none|serial|
|status|string|false|none|none|
|tx_bps|number|false|none|none|
|tx_bytes|number|false|none|none|
|tx_pkts|number|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|device type, ap / ble|
|uptime|number|false|none|how long, in seconds, has the device been up (or rebooted)|
|usb_stat|object|false|none|none|
|version|string|false|none|none|
|x|number|false|none|none|
|y|number|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|connected|
|status|disconnected|
|status|restarting|
|status|upgrading|

|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|splunk_token|string \| null|false|none|splunk token (If splunk_token is not defined for a type Splunk webhook, it will not send, regardless if the webhook receiver is configured to accept it.)|
|topics|[string]|false|none|N.B. For org webhooks, only device-events/alarms/audits/client-join/client-sessions/nac-sessions topics are supported.|

**N.B.**: Fields like `aps`, `bssids`, `ssids` are event specific. They are relevant to this event type ( rogue-ap-detected). For a different event type, different fields may be sent. These don’t contain all affected entities and are representative samples of entities (capped at 10). For marvis action related events, we expose `details` to include more event specific details.

Events specific fields for other alarm event type can be found with API https://api.mist.com/api/v1/const/alarm_defs, under “fields” array of /alarm_defs response object.

WLAN

**Note**: portal_template will be forked out of wlan objects soon. To fetch portal_template, please query portal_template_url. To update portal_template, use Wlan Portal Template.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acct_interim_interval|integer|false|none|how frequently should interim accounting be reported, 60-65535. default is 0 (use one specified in Access-Accept request from RADIUS Server). Very frequent messages can affect the performance of the radius server, 600 and up is recommended when enabled|
|acct_servers|[[acct_server](#schemaacct_server)]|false|none|list of RADIUS accounting servers, optional, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|airwatch|[wlan_airwatch](#schemawlan_airwatch)|false|none|airwatch wlan settings|
|allow_ipv6_ndp|boolean|false|none|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows or disallows ipv6 Neighbor Discovery packets to go through|
|allow_mdns|boolean|false|none|only applicable when limit_bcast==true, which allows mDNS / Bonjour packets to go through|
|allow_ssdp|boolean|false|none|only applicable when `limit_bcast`==`tru`e, which allows SSDP|
|ap_ids|[string(uuid)]|false|none|list of device ids|
|app_limit|object|false|none|bandwidth limiting for apps (applies to up/down)|
|app_qos|[wlan_app_qos](#schemawlan_app_qos)|false|none|app qos wlan settings|
|apply_to|string \| null|false|none|none|
|arp_filter|boolean|false|none|whether to enable smart arp filter|
|auth|[wlan_auth](#schemawlan_auth)|false|none|authentication wlan settings|
|auth_server_selection|string \| null|false|none|When ordered, AP will prefer and go back to the first server if possible|
|auth_servers|[[auth_server](#schemaauth_server)]|false|none|list of RADIUS authentication servers, at least one is needed if `auth type`==`eap`, order matters where the first one is treated as primary|
|auth_servers_nas_id|string \| null|false|none|optional, up to 48 bytes, will be dynamically generated if not provided. used only for authentication servers|
|auth_servers_nas_ip|string \| null|false|none|optional, NAS-IP-ADDRESS to use|
|auth_servers_retries|integer|false|none|radius auth session retries|
|auth_servers_timeout|integer|false|none|radius auth session timeout|
|band|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** `band` is deprecated and kept for backward compability. Use bands instead|
|band_steer|boolean|false|none|whether to enable band_steering, this works only when band==both|
|band_steer_force_band5|boolean|false|none|force dual-band capable client to connect to 5G|
|bands|[string]|false|none|list of radios that the wlan should apply to|
|block_blacklist_clients|boolean|false|none|whether to block the clients in the blacklist (up to first 256 macs)|
|bonjour|[wlan_bonjour](#schemawlan_bonjour)|false|none|bonjour gateway wlan settings|
|cisco_cwa|[wlan_cisco_cwa](#schemawlan_cisco_cwa)|false|none|Cisco CWA (central web authentication) required RADIUS with COA in order to work. See CWA: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/security/identity-services-engine/115732-central-web-auth-00.html<br>|
|client_limit_down|integer|false|none|kbps|
|client_limit_down_enabled|boolean|false|none|if downlink limiting per-client is enabled|
|client_limit_up|integer|false|none|kbps|
|client_limit_up_enabled|boolean|false|none|if uplink limiting per-client is enabled|
|coa_servers|[[coa_server](#schemacoa_server)]|false|none|list of COA (change of authorization) servers, optional|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|disable_11ax|boolean|false|none|some old WLAN drivers may not be compatible|
|disable_ht_vht_rates|boolean|false|none|to disable ht or vht rates|
|disable_uapsd|boolean|false|none|whether to disable U-APSD|
|disable_v1_roam_notify|boolean|false|none|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|disable_v2_roam_notify|boolean|false|none|disable sending v2 roam notification messages|
|disable_wmm|boolean|false|none|whether to disable WMM|
|dns_server_rewrite|object \| null|false|none|for radius_group-based DNS server (rewrite DNS request depending on the Group RADIUS server returns)|
|dtim|integer|false|none|none|
|dynamic_psk|object \| null|false|none|for dynamic PSK where we get per-user PSK from Radius<br>dynamic_psk allows PSK to be selected at runtime depending on context (wlan/site/user/...) thus following configurations are assumed (currently)<br>- PSK will come from RADIUS server<br>- AP sends client MAC as username ans password (i.e. `enable_mac_auth` is assumed)<br>- AP sends BSSID:SSID as Caller-Station-ID<br>- `auth_servers` is required<br>- PSK will come from cloud WLC if source is cloud_psks<br>- default_psk will be used if cloud WLC is not available<br>- `multi_psk_only` and `psk` is ignored<br>- `pairwise` can only be wpa2-ccmp (for now, wpa3 support on the roadmap)|
|dynamic_vlan|object \| null|false|none|for 802.1x|
|enable_local_keycaching|boolean|false|none|enable AP-AP keycaching via multicast|
|enable_wireless_bridging|boolean|false|none|whether to enable wireless bridging, which allows more broadcast packets to go through<br>(allows forwarding of DHCP response to client not associated with the AP)|

|for_site|boolean|false|read-only|none|

|hostname_ie|boolean|false|none|include hostname inside IE in AP beacons / probe responses|
|hotspot20|[wlan_hotspot_20](#schemawlan_hotspot_20)|false|none|hostspot 2.0 wlan settings|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|interface|string|false|none|where this WLAN will be connected to|
|isolation|boolean|false|none|whether to allow clients to talk to each other|
|l2_isolation|boolean|false|none|if isolation is enabled, whether to deny clients to talk to L2 on the LAN|
|legacy_overds|boolean|false|none|legacy devices requires the Over-DS (for Fast BSS Transition) bit set (while our chip doesn’t support it). Warning! Enabling this will cause problem for iOS devices.|
|limit_bcast|boolean|false|none|whether to limit broadcast packets going to wireless (i.e. only allow certain bcast packets to go through)|
|limit_probe_response|boolean|false|none|limit probe response base on some heuristic rules|
|max_idletime|integer|false|none|max idle time in seconds|
|mist_nac|object|false|none|none|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|msp_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|

|portal_image|string(uri) \| null|false|none|Url of portal background image|
|portal_sso_url|string \| null|false|none|none|
|portal_template_url|string \| null|false|none|N.B portal_template will be forked out of wlan objects soon. To fetch portal_template, please query portal_template_url. To update portal_template, use Wlan Portal Template.|
|qos|object|false|none|none|
|radsec|[radsec](#schemaradsec)|false|none|Radsec settings|
|rateset|object|false|none|none|
|roam_mode|string \| null|false|none|none|
|schedule|object|false|none|WLAN operating schedule, default is disabled|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|sle_excluded|boolean|false|none|whether to exclude this WLAN from SLE metrics|

|vlan_enabled|boolean|false|none|if vlan tagging is enabled|
|vlan_id|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|vlan_ids|[integer \| null]|false|none|list of VLAN ids|
|vlan_pooling|boolean|false|none|vlan pooling allows AP to place client on different VLAN using a deterministic algorithm|
|wlan_limit_down|integer|false|none|kbps|

<h2 id="tocS_wlan_datarates">wlan_datarates</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawlan_datarates"></a>
<a id="schema_wlan_datarates"></a>
<a id="tocSwlan_datarates"></a>
<a id="tocswlan_datarates"></a>

```json
{
  "ht": "string",
  "legacy": [
    "string"
  ],
  "min_rssi": 0,
  "template": "string",
  "vht": "string"
}
```

data rates wlan settings

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ht|string \| null|false|none|MCS bitmasks for 4 streams (16-bit for each stream, MCS0 is least significant bit), e.g. 00ff 00f0 001f limits HT rates to MCS 0-7 for 1 stream, MCS 4-7 for 2 stream (i.e. MCS 12-15), MCS 1-5 for 3 stream (i.e. MCS 16-20)|
|legacy|[string]|false|none|list of supported rates (IE=1) and extended supported rates (IE=50) for custom template, append ‘b’ at the end to indicate a rate being basic/mandatory. If `template`==`custom` is configured and legacy does not define at least one basic rate, it will use `no-legacy` default values|
|min_rssi|integer|false|none|Minimum RSSI for client to connect, 0 means not enforcing|
|template|string \| null|false|none|* `no-legacy`: no 11b<br>* `compatible`: all, like before, default setting that Broadcom/Atheros used<br>* `legacy-only`: disable 802.11n and 802.11ac <br>* `high-density`: no 11b, no low rates<br>* `custom`: user defined|
|vht|string|false|none|MCS bitmasks for 4 streams (16-bit for each stream, MCS0 is least significant bit), e.g. 03ff 01ff 00ff limits VHT rates to MCS 0-9 for 1 stream, MCS 0-8 for 2 streams, and MCS 0-7 for 3 streams.|

```json
{
  "created_time": 0,
  "for_site": true,
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "last_ips": [
    "string"
  ],
  "mac": "string",
  "match": "ap_id",
  "modified_time": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "op": "in",
  "org_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "resource_mac": "string",
  "services": [
    "string"
  ],
  "site_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "specs": [
    {
      "port_range": "0",
      "protocol": "any",
      "subnets": [
        "0.0.0.0/0"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "subnet": "string",
  "type": "match",
  "values": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

WxLAN Tag
* type:
** client: created manually (e.g. on wireless client table, when they spot a device of interest, they can create an wxlan tag for it
** resource: created automatically when we discover a network resource
** subnet: create automatically when a subnet is discovered

* match:
** wlan_id, ap_id: values are a list of Wlan / Device ids
** client_mac: values are a list of MAC addresses

* radius_group: this is a smart tag that matches RADIUS-Filter-ID, Airespace-ACL-Name (VendorID=14179, VendorType=6) / Aruba-User-Role (VendorID=14823, VendorType=1)
* radius_username: this matches the ATTR-User-Name(1)
* radius_class: thie matches the ATTR-Class(25)
* radius_attr: the values are [ “6=1”, “26=10.2.3.4” ], this support other RADIUS attributes where we know the type
* radius_vendor: the values are [ “14179.10=1”, “14178.16=1.2.3.4” ], this matches vendor attributes and will be dynamically evaluated

|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|last_ips|[string]|false|none|none|
|mac|string \| null|false|none|none|
|match|string \| null|false|none|none|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|name|string|true|none|The name|
|op|string|false|none|none|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|resource_mac|string \| null|false|none|none|
|services|[string]|false|none|none|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|specs|[object]|false|none|none|
|subnet|string|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|values|[string]|false|none|list of values to match|

WxLAn Tunnel

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|dmvpn|object|false|none|Dynamic Multipoint VPN configurations|
|for_mgmt|boolean|false|none|determined during creation time and cannot be toggled. A management tunnel cannot be used by wxlan rule or by wlan|
|for_site|boolean|false|read-only|none|
|hello_interval|integer|false|none|in seconds, used as heartbeat to detect if a tunnel is alive. AP will try another peer after missing N hellos specified by hello_retries.|
|hello_retries|integer|false|none|none|
|hostname|string|false|none|optional, overwrite the hostname in SCCRQ control message, default is “” or null, %H and %M can be used, which will be replace with corresponding values:<br>* %H: name of the ap if provided (and will be stripped so it can be used for hostname) and fallbacks to MAC<br>* %M: MAC (e.g. 5c5b350e0060)|
|id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|ipsec|object|false|none|IPSec-related configurations; requires DMVPN be enabled|
|is_static|boolean|false|none|whether it’s static/unmanaged (i.e. no control session). As the session configurations are not compatible, cannot be toggled.|
|modified_time|number|false|read-only|none|
|mtu|integer|false|none|0 to enable PMTU, 552-1500 to start PMTU with a lower MTU|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the tunnel|
|org_id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|peers|[string]|false|none|list of remote peers’ IP or hostname|
|router_id|string|false|none|optional, overwrite the router-id in SCCRQ control message, default is “0” or null, can also be an IPv4 address|
|secret|string|false|none|secret, ‘’ if no auth is used|
|sessions|[object]|false|none|sessions to be established with the tunnel. Has to be >= 1 in order for this tunnel to be useful. For management tunnel, it can only have 1|
|site_id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|none|
|udp_port|integer|false|none|udp port if `use_udp`==`true`|
|use_udp|boolean|false|none|whether to use UDP instead of IP (proto=115, which is default of L2TPv3)|
